concepts.title: The Only Thing Anyone Has Ever Loved
concepts.description: affection reduced to ownership, then to identity, then devotion recovered from the reduction; the volume's flattest mechanism for the gopīs' pre-eminence

concepts.title: The Serpent Who Blamed the Maker and Got Away With It
concepts.description: the strongest determinist argument in the volume, spoken to God about the crime, answered with relocation and immunity rather than rebuttal

concepts.title: The Game Was Built for One Player
concepts.description: an assassin recognised, accepted as a friend, and killed by a rule invented for the purpose; the trap made entirely of true components

concepts.title: Forty Verdicts Delivered as Weather

concepts.description: the vastra-haraṇa held without softening: the narrator's *"as if they were puppets"* and the contentment clause four words apart, and no bridge between them

concepts.title: The Seed That Stays a Seed
concepts.description: a desire-driven practice stops producing desire; the seed is not removed but rendered infertile by contact, and stays a seed

concepts.title: The Men Who Had Every Qualification

concepts.title: Three Moves to Take a God's Sacrifice
concepts.description: an argument that no deity confers fruits, followed by the manufacture of one that eats the offerings and threatens the neighbours

concepts.title: The God Who Kept His Job
concepts.description: the volume's only god who surrenders authority without losing office; the deposed incumbent supplies the title and draws the jurisdictional line himself

concepts.title: The Question Nobody Asked Out Loud
concepts.description: an unvoiced wish read and granted in full; the entrance requirement is stated and waived in consecutive sentences

title: V3-B. The Rāsa, and the Non-Imitation Clause

concepts.title: He Argued Against It First
concepts.description: a complete orthodox strīdharma lecture delivered to the women who just abandoned it, extending to a ban on hearing, seeing, meditating, loving and chanting; they win by applying his own rule to its right object

concepts.title: The Women Who Never Got Out of the House
concepts.description: the gopīs who were shut in attain final liberation on the spot, in one clause, while the ones who attended are still grieving at 10(82)

concepts.title: It Doesn't Matter How You Feel About Him
concepts.description: desire, anger, fear, identity and affection listed as equivalent inputs; the gopīs defended by the argument that hatred already works

concepts.title: What Was on the Stove
concepts.description: devotion measured in interrupted processes rather than surrendered goods, and most of the cost borne by people not in the scene

concepts.title: They Started Playing Him
concepts.description: deprived of him they operate him, casting every rescue scene and never themselves; identity by performance rather than merger

concepts.title: Reading the Ground
concepts.description: a five-step forensic reconstruction of the evening they were excluded from, correct in every inference; then the woman who was chosen is abandoned for the same fault

concepts.title: The Love Song With a Charge In It
concepts.description: the Gopī-gīta as devotional set-piece and charge-sheet in one document, delivered by a voice the translation cannot attribute

concepts.title: He Explains Why He Withholds
concepts.description: mutual love classed as *"selfishness and nothing else"*, withholding named as method, and a debt conceded and declared unpayable

concepts.title: Do What He Says, Not What He Did
concepts.description: the transgression conceded, the exemption argued two incompatible ways, and a firewall installed between the hero's speech and his conduct

title: V3-C. Separation as an Engineered Condition

concepts.title: The Version He Gives When Nobody Is Objecting
concepts.description: the only account of the rāsa in the volume with no defence attached, delivered in private to a minister with nothing at stake

concepts.title: The Charges Against God, Delivered to an Insect

concepts.title: The Consolation That Dissolves the Loss

concepts.title: The Envoy Who Asked to Be Vegetation

concepts.title: The Skandha Ends by Doing It Again

concepts.title: The Woman Who Was Straightened
concepts.description: a cure nobody asked for, desire listed among the things the new body produced, the wish granted and graded as ignorant in the same breath

concepts.title: The Galleries Convict the Room

concepts.title: The Refusal That Kept the Power

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta (Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja, Bhaktivedanta 1975 edition) — Phase 2, Cluster B

concepts.title: The Three Confidential Desires
concepts.description: an omnipotent God blocked not by a limit on power but by a limit on position, and the public reason for the descent demoted to "external" one chapter after being announced

concepts.title: Majesty Weakens Love
concepts.description: Kṛṣṇa names reverence itself as the obstacle to the love he wants; Yaśodā's rope, Arjuna's apology, and a father told his son is God who declines the information

concepts.title: Kāma and Prema: The Direction Test
concepts.description: one axis, no second criterion: whose senses are being served. Identical acts, opposite categories, and the moment the tradition adopts a test nobody but the defendant can check

concepts.title: Āśraya and Viṣaya: The Abode Enjoys More
concepts.description: the holder of love outstrips its object ten million to one, which puts the best seat in the cosmology outside God and reranks service above union everywhere in the corpus

concepts.title: Devotees Angry at Their Own Ecstasy
concepts.description: Dāruka resents the love that stiffened his arms and stopped his fanning; the tradition's proofs of attainment and its marks of failure turn out to be the same signs

concepts.title: The Mirror Competition
concepts.description: her love and his sweetness each increasing in response to the other, "neither knows defeat": an unbounded feedback loop with the three brakes that stop every real instance quietly removed

concepts.title: Rādhā as Teacher, Kṛṣṇa as Pupil
concepts.description: the corpus's supreme teaching relationship has no lineage, no content, no submission and no qualification, and breaks every rule the same tradition enforces about teaching

concepts.title: The Contradictions of Rādhā's Prema
concepts.description: all-pervading yet expanding, supreme yet prideless, spotless yet crooked; contradictions offered as the description rather than confessed as its limits

concepts.title: Refusing the Five Liberations
concepts.description: five genuine prizes declined with the offer stipulated as real, because every one of them is a promotion out of the enriched seat

concepts.title: The Esotericism Gate
concepts.description: a filter on application implemented as a filter on comprehension, and a 1975 edition that preserved the doctrine while dismantling its protection

concepts.title: Rādhā as the Source of All Consorts
concepts.description: goddesses of fortune as her portions, queens of Dvārakā as her reflections, a name read out of a verb; uniqueness at the top bought by spending interiority at the bottom

concepts.title: Caitanya Mahāprabhu: The Combined Form
concepts.description: Kṛṣṇa carrying Rādhā's sentiment and complexion; the identity claim and the appearance claim are one claim, and four hundred pages of reported behaviour follow from it

concepts.title: Six Diversities in One
concepts.description: six ontological categories collapsed into one truth in the opening verse, with the author's own numbered map of his invocation; identity framings license unlimited penalties where complementary ones produce development

concepts.title: All the Names Are Correct
concepts.description: a doctrine defended to the death against outsiders and declared optional among insiders; a proposition whose truth-value moves with the speaker is a shibboleth, not a belief

concepts.title: Channa-avatāra: The Concealed Descent
concepts.description: deliberate self-concealment, the owls that cannot see the sun, and renunciation described in the first person as an inducement; deniability trades accountability for legibility

concepts.title: He Refuses the Identification
concepts.description: four refusals of the book's own thesis, in a community where refusal is the highest-status move available; a humility-valuing tradition destroys its ability to read its own members

concepts.title: I Do Not Dance by My Own Will
concepts.description: disclaimed agency at n=4 across four centuries of one lineage; earned automaticity and possession share a sentence and only one of them can be credited

concepts.title: The Nṛsiṁha Mood and the Fear Offence
concepts.description: an ecstatic state halted because "causing fear among people is an offense"; the corpus's one consequentialist sentence, never enumerated among its formal offences

concepts.title: The Army of Associates
concepts.description: the entire order of battle retained with associates as soldiers and limbs as weapons; an abstract enemy is safe only while the weapons are abstract too

concepts.title: Advaita Ācārya and the Summons
concepts.description: a devotee reverse-engineers the terms of divine reciprocity and forces an incarnation; obligation without a ceiling comes from a gift the recipient cannot repay in kind

concepts.title: Advaita as Material Cause
concepts.description: *nimitta* and *upādāna*, the anti-Sāṅkhya claim that creation never arises from dead matter, and limb rather than part; the dichotomy has no room for a substrate that shapes without participating

concepts.title: The Mutual Subordination
concepts.description: a permanent deadlock in which each man insists on serving the other, with Nanda Mahārāja as the case that has no exemptions; downward competition stays honest only while descending stays expensive

concepts.title: Guru-tattva: The Initiator and the Instructors
concepts.description: the one who lets you in and the ones you learned from, declared identical; a lineage claim is useful exactly to the degree it can be checked

concepts.title: Sweetness Over Opulence
concepts.description: the majestic expansions defect and the goddess of fortune fails to enter Vṛndāvana; devaluation and inconvertibility are different failures and demand opposite responses

concepts.title: Which Brahmā?
concepts.description: a correction delivered as an admin query, a hall of private audiences, and the measurement that makes ours the smallest; rank is a two-variable function and the ranked party controls neither

concepts.title: The Moon Society of Kṛṣṇa's Face
concepts.description: an itemised allegorical inventory that ends in a marketplace; memory *for* a reader and memory *by* a reader call for opposite techniques

concepts.title: The Three Dhāmas and the Virajā
concepts.description: three regions, a three-to-one proportion, and a boundary that is a river rather than a wall; wall cosmologies produce escape logic and river cosmologies produce relocation

concepts.title: The Pañca-tattva
concepts.description: five features, all of them devotee-categories, with no slot for God and an open fifth place the reader occupies; distributed authorship buys generativity and pays in having nothing to adjudicate with

concepts.title: The Inundation and Those Who Fled
concepts.description: a flood dodged by the trained, and renunciation adopted as a device to reach them; a credential's power is the obligation it imposes on others, not the competence it certifies

concepts.title: The Guru Called Me a Fool
concepts.description: the tradition's central practice originates in a disqualification; a damaging assessment calcifies into identity when it ends in a verdict and not when it ends in a task

concepts.title: The Author's Own Conversion
concepts.description: the corpus's provenance begins with the author siding against his brother and the brother falling down; the middle position closed, and the last man to hold it made the demonstration

concepts.title: Half-a-Hen Logic
concepts.description: selective acceptance as a category error, and whole rejection ranked above partial; the test is whether the part you kept still works

concepts.title: Nityānanda as Balarāma
concepts.description: the second body serving the first in three rotating modes; role fluidity is a by-product of genuine equality and cannot be staffed

concepts.title: The Bhakti-vṛkṣa
concepts.description: delegation justified by a stated throughput limit, a universal commission, and a reputational motive said out loud; the architecture that lets a movement scale is the one it uses to purge

concepts.title: Remembering the Names Liberates
concepts.description: three chapters of enumeration as practice rather than appendix; body-encoded sequences outperform semantic ones, and this vault's compression of them is costed on the page

concepts.title: The Branches That Withered
concepts.description: a succession ruling written in botany and filed inside a liturgy; botanical verbs remove agents, and a ruling recited as devotion is never argued with

concepts.title: The Kamalākānta Affair
concepts.description: a flat prohibition on clerical patronage argued on an interior ground and a reputational one; the cost of accepting is paid at acceptance, in information

concepts.title: Nāmābhāsa and the Yavanas
concepts.description: potency in the syllables, and the boundary in the same speech: no intent works, wrong intent does not. The most easily botched point in the corpus

concepts.title: The Tongue That Would Not Stop
concepts.description: mockers who cannot stop chanting; attack requires reproduction, reproduction is rehearsal, and opponents propagate a phrase faster than adherents

concepts.title: The Plundered Storehouse
concepts.description: a sealed treasury looted and distributed with no test of fitness, and a supply that increases as it is given; abundance has to be signalled by transgression rather than by cost

concepts.title: The Hindu Complaint
concepts.description: the tradition's own neighbours argue that broadcasting the name exhausts it; almost every fight about widening access is a disguised disagreement about the category of the good

concepts.title: If All Were Liberated, the Universe Would Empty
concepts.description: universal salvation objected to on population grounds, and answered by conservation; conservation claims reassure precisely because the worrying case is undefined

concepts.title: The Echo That Is Not an Echo
concepts.description: trees chanting rather than reflecting; a disagreement can be located in the seer or in the seen, and only one of those can be wrong

concepts.title: Kīrtana Among the Untouchables
concepts.description: a boundary crossed at its jurisdiction rather than its definition, and the word kept in the sentence that celebrates the crossing

concepts.title: The Chand Kazi Confrontation
concepts.description: capacity made visible and then declined; a demonstration that consists of the banned act has no edge for an administrator to police

concepts.title: The Kinship Gambit
concepts.description: de-escalation by producing a prior relationship; a participant can only re-orient by precedence, never by novelty

concepts.title: The Cow Argument and the Koran
concepts.description: ⚠️ flagged page, flag in the body: a partisan writes an opponent's capitulation, and a concession that runs past the point to the grounds is the signature of construction

concepts.title: The Lion Dream
concepts.description: supernatural enforcement narrated by the opponent with marks offered for inspection and never inspected; unfalsifiable criteria govern insiders and inspectable phenomena recruit outsiders

concepts.title: The Seven-Day Silence
concepts.description: a refutation with no proposition in it; silence acquires force in proportion to what the other party keeps saying into it

concepts.title: Direct-Meaning Hermeneutics
concepts.description: plain sense as the whole basis of authority, tested on a deliberately costly case; a rule about who bears the burden of a reading, and an anti-clerical instrument by accident

concepts.title: Śaṅkarācārya Was Under Orders
concepts.description: the chief opponent reclassified as a divine agent; an assigned devil buys interpretive security and forecloses learning anything from the opposition

concepts.title: The Māyāvāda Refutation
concepts.description: *pariṇāma* against *vivarta*, the touchstone, and a rival ranked more dangerous for accepting your scriptures than for rejecting them

concepts.title: Tri-yuga: No Avatāra in Kali
concepts.description: a categorical exclusion met by a sub-category; the test that separates a refinement from moved goalposts is whether the distinction predates the case

concepts.title: Sannyāsa Rank and Sampradāya
concepts.description: an offer to re-initiate God into a better lineage; a credential admits and files at once, and the ordinary failure is an honest credential producing an assessment with no content

concepts.title: Mercy, Not Logic
concepts.description: expertise as active obstruction; the hardest beliefs to examine are the ones acquired at cost, not the ones absorbed unconsciously

concepts.title: The Ātmārāma Verse, Eighteen Ways
concepts.description: nine readings answered by eighteen that touch none of them; virtuosity in a generative method is evidence about the operator and nothing about the material

concepts.title: Mukti-pada or Bhakti-pada
concepts.description: a word the tradition dislikes, kept in scripture because it is there; an inconvenient retention is the only checkable evidence of editorial constraint

concepts.title: The Six Philosophies and the Mahājana Path
concepts.description: argument declared incapable in a chapter won by argument; an epistemology that defers to authority *because reasoning fails* disables its own error-correction

concepts.title: The Bhāgavatam as the Vedānta Commentary
concepts.description: the author's own gloss as the commentary that is not one; self-commentary is strong evidence about intent and none about meaning

concepts.title: The Eho Bāhya Ladder
concepts.description: eleven correct answers refused without explanation; each rung reached by dropping what made the last one work, and refusal used as a pump rather than a gate

concepts.title: Authority by Knowledge, Not Birth
concepts.description: the tradition's most-quoted egalitarian verse, staged as a contact act in front of the people best qualified to object; a principle is only demonstrated where it was expensive to hold

concepts.title: Sakhī-bhāva: Vicarious Joy
concepts.description: the arranger's happiness at ten million times the participant's; the enriched position rather than the selfless one, and what separates the paid carer from the depleted one

concepts.title: Rādhā's Ornament Allegory
concepts.description: an emotional inventory ordered by distance from the skin; to make an unordered set memorable, map it onto a sequence the reader already performs

concepts.title: Prema-vilāsa-vivarta
concepts.description: the summit stopped by a hand over the mouth; a terminus that certifies the ladder and cannot be assessed, and the only union available where nothing arrives

concepts.title: Hlādinī, Sandhinī, Samvit
concepts.description: existence, knowledge and pleasure as three functions of one potency; the third item is where a tradition's actual commitments live

concepts.title: Kṛṣṇa Attracted to Himself
concepts.description: the reflection in the pillar; the two ordinary routes to seeing yourself from outside are reconstruction and error, and there is no third

concepts.title: Kṛṣṇa as Debtor
concepts.description: the one advertised exception to proportional reciprocation; obligations are permanent exactly when the currency is inconvertible

concepts.title: The Śrutis Took Gopī Bodies
concepts.description: scripture abandoning its own method; before another decade of refinement, check whether the people who have the thing got it your way

concepts.title: Rāmānanda as Instrument
concepts.description: the puppet and the stringed instrument; only the second concedes that the material determines the sound, and it is the one both a devotional and a craft account can accept

concepts.title: The Mahā-bhāgavata Vision
concepts.description: seeing without seeing forms; perception differs in sorting as well as in valuing, and only the second is negotiable by conversation

concepts.title: The Bhakti-latā-bīja
concepts.description: the creeper, the seed and the watering; a metaphor whose failure modes match its subject's, with an institution built into its first move

concepts.title: The Weeds Beside the Creeper
concepts.description: the same water feeds everything, liberation is on the weed list, and a successful practice generates its own endemic weeds

concepts.title: The Mad Elephant Offence
concepts.description: one instance, total loss, and a fence rather than a discipline; catastrophic rules concentrate discretion rather than eliminating it

concepts.title: Sādhana Awakens What Is Already There
concepts.description: love uncovered rather than produced; a doctrine that guarantees the equipment is a doctrine in which every failure is yours

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta — Cluster G continued, 2026-08-14 (PARTIAL, 12 pages)

concepts.title: The Funnel of the Fortunate
concepts.description: 8,400,000 species narrowing to one pure devotee among millions of liberated souls; a ranking wearing a headcount, whose load-bearing step swaps one set for another

concepts.title: Kṛṣṇa Withholds What You Ask For
concepts.description: the deliberately unanswered prayer argued as intelligence rather than mercy, and the one thing hidden because giving it would bind the giver

concepts.title: The Log on the River
concepts.description: deliverance as an accident happening to cargo, in a chapter devoted to method; and a river this metaphysics cannot let be indifferent

concepts.title: The Six Limbs of Śaraṇāgati
concepts.description: four performable actions and two required beliefs, listed as one kind of thing, with a guarantee resting on a qualifier no observer can assess

concepts.title: Caitya-guru and the External Ācārya
concepts.description: the teacher inside and the teacher outside declared one person, which abolishes the legitimate disagreement without issuing a rule about obedience

concepts.title: The Two Formidable Enemies
concepts.description: better bars and burning flames than the company of non-devotees; environment advice and exclusion advice are the same advice pointed at different objects. Carries the SIGNAL

concepts.title: Good Qualities Follow Bhakti
concepts.description: water the root, feed the stomach; virtues as byproducts. Excellent advice about where to spend effort and a terrible instrument for judging anybody

concepts.title: Jīvera Svarūpa: Kṛṣṇera Nitya-dāsa
concepts.description: the most-quoted line in the book, and a description rather than an instruction; the sentence that removes your standing to object also makes you impossible to expel

concepts.title: Sambandha, Abhidheya, Prayojana
concepts.description: relationship, process, goal, in that order; the destination disclosed after the point where a student could still check the method against it

concepts.title: The Astrologer and the Buried Treasure
concepts.description: wasps, a ghost and a black snake for the three respectable disciplines; knowing where the treasure is turns out to be the setup, not the answer

concepts.title: Viparyayo 'Smṛtiḥ
concepts.description: not error but reversed memory, servant remembered as competitor; a diagnosis that converts every objection into a specimen of itself

concepts.title: Rati-ābhāsa
concepts.description: the counterfeit nobody is faking: real symptoms from the wrong root, sorted by an expert with no stated criterion. A semblance of the name works; a semblance of attachment does not

concepts.title: The Expansion Taxonomy
concepts.description: twenty-four forms distinguished solely by the order of four identical weapons in four identical hands; identity by permutation, inside a corpus whose every other distinction ranks by fullness

concepts.title: The Sādhu Inquires Though He Knows
concepts.description: the chapter declaring its own instruction a formality from inside it, and carrying on unchanged; a device that survives disclosure was never trading on concealment

concepts.title: The Nine Anubhāvas of Sprouted Bhāva
concepts.description: the corpus's best diagnostic and its dullest; seven checkable signs in the same chapter that rules visible signs uninformative

concepts.title: The Ātmārāma Verse, Sixty-One Ways
concepts.description: a combinatorial method with no stopping condition, performed for a student already convinced; abundance of interpretation is a fact about the interpreter until somebody runs the control

concepts.title: Nārada and the Hunter
concepts.description: harm reduction negotiated before the profession is addressed, subsistence guaranteed before the bow is broken, and a convert who ends up gentler and poorer than the instruction required

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta — Cluster H, Purī: Festival, Kingship and Ritual Order, 2026-08-14 (PARTIAL, 8 pages)

concepts.title: The Guṇḍicā Cleaning
concepts.description: a hundred pots and brooms, two passes, quality measured by the size of your dust pile with the Lord's the largest; a scene that travels from job to discipline to play in one afternoon, and an exemption list of five that photographs the hierarchy it suspends

concepts.title: The Bengali Who Drank the Footwater
concepts.description: performed anger, performed enforcement and a pre-arranged pardon, disclosed to the reader in advance; the corpus's formula for marking staged severity, and the chapter where it is not used

concepts.title: Refusing the King
concepts.description: *"still to be considered a venomous snake"*, an exploit designed by the Lord's own confidant, and a fiction of ignorance that lets a rule be technically kept while substantively broken. Merged with `the-workaround` as declared

concepts.title: The Prince as Proxy
concepts.description: a stated doctrine of representation issued to permit exactly what the rule forbids, by the person who issued the rule; and a boy nobody asks about

concepts.title: The Ratha-yātrā Dancing
concepts.description: seven divisions, fourteen drums, every group certain it has him exclusively, and the banned king holding the outer cordon. The partition produced the effect, not the centre

concepts.title: The Three Grades of Vaiṣṇava by Effect
concepts.description: the corpus's one checkable criterion, observable by anybody and capable of coming out negative, used nowhere it would have decided something

concepts.title: Vāsudeva Datta's Petition
concepts.description: universal substitutionary atonement offered by the substitute and refused with a she-goat; the same chapter puts him under financial supervision

concepts.title: The Lord Refuses to Intervene
concepts.description: four deputations refused, *"the revenue of the government is more sacred than the property of a brāhmaṇa"*, and a life saved by a bureaucrat's cost-benefit argument and credited to Jagannātha

concepts.title: Govinda in the Doorway
concepts.description: a servant applying the direction-of-benefit criterion more precisely than the chapter that states it, inside a scene the narrator admits was engineered

concepts.title: Care as Containment
concepts.description: seven instances, five authors, one mechanism and no word for it; a community managing its founder against his own impulses and calling every instance service

concepts.title: The Servants of the Household
concepts.description: a hundred people's worth of hoarded food, a servant asking to be released from a position, and three directions of untruth all clean by the corpus's own test

concepts.title: The Negotiated Invitation
concepts.description: a religious principle refused in the register of principle and conceded in the register of quantity, in one conversation

concepts.title: Prasāda and the Collapse of Purity Rules
concepts.description: the most polluting category in the ritual order redefined as the most purifying, by doing rather than arguing; and a conversion that needed no doctrine

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta — Cluster I, The Discipline Cases, 2026-08-14 (COMPLETE, 14 pages)

concepts.title: Harder Than a Thunderbolt, Softer Than a Flower
concepts.description: the corpus's own doctrine of its protagonist's inconsistency, supplied by the narrator where the record is least defensible; it converts every counter-example into evidence and removes the one argument any advocate would have

concepts.title: The Prerogative Doctrine
concepts.description: a named personal exemption grounded in a state *"he alone, and no one else, can understand,"* with the bar on generalising stated in the same breath

concepts.title: Rāmadāsa Viśvāsa
concepts.description: flawless conduct refused on an invisible interior state, by a verdict consisting of nothing happening; the commonest disciplinary instrument there is, and the only one with nothing to appeal against

concepts.title: The Expulsion of Junior Haridāsa
concepts.description: ⚠️ flagged page, flag in the body. An errand, a year of refused appeals, a drowning and a smile, with the Layer A silence and the Layer B deterrence rationale shown side by side

concepts.title: Haridāsa's Chosen Death
concepts.description: the declared pair: a death chosen in its moment, a corpse carried on the Lord's lap, a sea consecrated, and a man who names a shared plate as the summit of his life

concepts.title: The Dismissal of Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa
concepts.description: a graver offence, a public dismissal, and four men who invented an errand and asked permission for *a person*; the strongest evidence that the Antya 2 severity was chosen

concepts.title: The Licensed and Unlicensed Critic
concepts.description: the appointed critic honoured and posted four hundred miles away; the unlicensed one changes the Lord's behaviour and is defended by his victim

concepts.title: Mādhavendra Purī's Death
concepts.description: one disciple brings correct philosophy and is cursed, the other cleans his guru's stool and is blessed, and the whole tradition descends through the second

concepts.title: Vallabha Bhaṭṭa's Freeze-Out
concepts.description: no refutation, no ruling, no accountable party, and a hundred independent inferences; the anatomy of a social death, recorded approvingly

concepts.title: His Associates Are Extremely Critical
concepts.description: a senior devotee unafraid of God and afraid of the movement, certified blameless by the narrator, and right

concepts.title: Svarūpa Dāmodara Forbids the Commentary
concepts.description: a text classed as a hazard rather than an error, with confidence in one's own resistance named as the symptom

concepts.title: The Two Rules and the Selective Critic
concepts.description: a two-part rule kept at the half that costs nothing, by somebody not choosing and unable to see it

concepts.title: The Devadāsī's Song
concepts.description: running through thorns toward a voice whose sex he did not know, and a standing bodyguard order issued afterwards; a rule aimed at a category the person in the state cannot perceive

concepts.title: Three and a Half Intimate Devotees
concepts.description: a woman accepted as an associate of Rādhārāṇī counted as half a person, in the same chapter as the expulsion of the man who fetched rice from her

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta — Cluster J, Renunciation and the Vṛndāvana Retrieval, 2026-08-14 (COMPLETE, 15 pages)

concepts.title: Renunciation as a Logistics Problem
concepts.description: capital moved in advance, a false pretext aimed at the one person who could have stopped it, and months of accumulated ordinariness before the walk; three men, three fortunes, one method, and a doctrine that never describes the entry

concepts.title: Sanātana's Escape
concepts.description: seven thousand gold coins to a jailer, a cover story supplied to the man taking the risk, and a landlord who admits he would have killed for the gold and is pressed to take it anyway; renunciation as professional work

concepts.title: The Muslim Mendicant at the Door
concepts.description: one man reported two ways by two observers at a doorway, a self-misreading refused by claiming the benefit rather than granting a dispensation, and a shave ordered twenty lines after birth is declared irrelevant

concepts.title: The Blanket and the Torn Quilt
concepts.description: correction delivered by repeated glance and explained only after compliance; and the reason that actually moved the blanket, which is not renunciation but ridicule

concepts.title: The Epilepsy Cover Story
concepts.description: the corpus's central evidence named as a disease by its own subject, to a patrol whose reasoning was sound, with four men's lives on the sentence; a partisan text preserving the readings that damage it

concepts.title: The Pāṭhān Conversion from the Koran
concepts.description: ⚠️ flagged page, flag in the body. What this text claims a Muslim ascetic conceded, and why the tell is the second move: a complexion, not a hermeneutic — a destination equipped with an exegesis

concepts.title: Your Body Is My Property
concepts.description: the law of bailment applied to a man's body without softening, argued to a third party in his hearing; a consolation that concedes his whole case about himself and denies him the decision

concepts.title: The Hot Sand and the Siṁha-dvāra
concepts.description: blistered soles at noon to spare temple servants a contamination the theology denies exists, and a ruling that voids the rule and endorses it in one sentence

concepts.title: Anupama's Refusal
concepts.description: the tradition itself declined on the ground of a completed prior sale, and the refusal embraced and matched with a precedent; a doctrine of legitimate refusal stated twice and never used again

concepts.title: The Excavation of Gopāla
concepts.description: a god complains of cold and two years later there is a temple, a priesthood and thousands of cows gathered one per household; a construction log with a dream at the top, and a burial whose political cause is stated once

concepts.title: Sākṣi-gopāla the Witness
concepts.description: a promise witnessed by a Deity, a village assembly, and a settlement written in black and white with both signatures taken; the atheist signs because he is certain the witness cannot appear, and the god is out-argued from his own precedent

concepts.title: The Deity as Mobile Asset
concepts.description: buried under a raid, transferred on a stated plea the text itself corrects, carried off by a conquering king; three forms of force and every relocation narrated as the god's own choosing, with the pretext disclosed only where the concealed motive was trivial

concepts.title: The Offering Eaten and Intact
concepts.description: food consumed and undiminished at Govardhana, in Śacī's pots and in Nṛsiṁhānanda's three dinners, and in all three a witness doubts and is later confirmed unprompted; the strongest evidential form available and the least auditable, which are one property

concepts.title: The Cidā-dadhi Festival
concepts.description: two pots per person for an uncountable crowd, people standing in the Ganges because the bank ran out, and the shopkeepers bought out and fed their own stock back; hospitality engineered to leave no ledger

concepts.title: The Chain of Hearing
concepts.description: transmission as pure propagation with no initiation, qualification or filter, against Ādi 1's full dīkṣā apparatus, and the same word — *paramparā* — used for both

title: ⚑ Kalyāṇ Hanumān Aṅka (Gītā Press 1975, Mahavir Aaradhyaa English rendering) — Hanumanic Strategy build

concepts.title: Ardha-Kukkuṭī-Nyāya — The Half-Hen Fallacy
concepts.description: the prohibition on selectively accepting a source whose authority you have already conceded; the concession, not the selection, is where the error is set

concepts.title: Arthavāda — Reading Scripture for Intent, Not Narrative
concepts.description: Pūrva Mīmāṃsā's published licence for non-literal reading, its three subdivisions, and the external-contradiction requirement that keeps it honest

concepts.title: Three Births, Three Kalpas — Plurality Without Adjudication
concepts.description: incompatible origin accounts distributed across world-cycles rather than ranked; what the device protects and what it costs

concepts.title: Swallowing the Sun as Siddhi, Not Hyperbole
concepts.description: the identity-suspends-scale defence, the *Yoga Sūtra* ladder, and the episode read as a targeted lesson to Sūrya and Rāhu

concepts.title: The Maṅgala Paradox — Ill Omen and Embodied Auspiciousness
concepts.description: Tulsīdās calling him both at once; substance ranked over omen

concepts.title: The Twelve Names of Hanuman
concepts.description: the *Ānanda Rāmāyaṇa* protective list, deed-anchored naming, and the three thresholds it is said at

concepts.title: A Body Kept by Choice — The Two Liberations
concepts.description: souls freed by knowledge dissolve, souls freed by devotion keep a form that is eternal but chosen rather than required

concepts.title: The Eight Fruits of Remembrance
concepts.description: *Ānanda Rāmāyaṇa* Manohara-kāṇḍa 13.16, quoted independently by two Śaṅkarācāryas; a promise specific enough to audit, and the correction that it is not in the Chalisa

concepts.title: The Eight Siddhis Mapped to Episodes
concepts.description: the complete mapping, the point where it switches from feats to dispositions, and the relocation of *vaśitva* from summit to foundation

concepts.title: God Is Mine, or I Am God's
concepts.description: Rāmsukhdās on two devotions that are behaviourally identical while things go well, and the refusal needed to tell them apart

concepts.title: The Name as Compressed Biography
concepts.description: the root read as character, function and origin at once; the species objection that should have sunk the standard derivation; and the missing constraint the method never supplies

concepts.title: The Wind-Names Are Not Synonyms
concepts.description: four names, three registers, and the doctrine that what returns is shaped by which name you used

concepts.title: Fractional or Entire — The Rudra Identity Dispute
concepts.description: Śvetāśvatara 3.2 against the eleventh-Rudra reading, Nandi's curse as a third causal register, and the theodicy that collapses if the fraction goes

concepts.title: Seven Registers of One Devotion
concepts.description: memory, vow, joy, speed, roar, battle-cry and wrath as one devotion at seven pitches, with the collateral cost left on the page

concepts.title: Restraint Was Rāma Managing Him
concepts.description: the offers nobody takes up, and the reading in which the celebrated humility is an administrative outcome

concepts.title: The Drowned Epic
concepts.description: the one thing nobody can renounce, renounced in ninety seconds, and the accounting that made it possible

concepts.title: The Fierce Register and Its Guardrails
concepts.description: the twelve-syllable *rudrātmakāya* mantra, the six rites turned inward, and the Śaṅkarācārya who says do not

concepts.title: The Vanara Civilisation Argument
concepts.description: courts, funeral rites and Vedic grammar against *animals by birth*; three positions across two contributors, and the translation habit that keeps the question alive

concepts.title: Nīlakaṇṭha's Vedic Hanuman
concepts.description: the *Mantra-Rāmāyaṇa* reading Ṛgveda 9.73.7 and 10.64.8 as naming him; a transparent retrofit, and what would actually confirm it

concepts.title: Kiṣkindhā as Kāśī
concepts.description: Śivlāl Pāṭhak transposing a whole *kāṇḍa* onto Vārāṇasī; a commentary on the *Mānas* and not on Vālmīki, and the structural reading that survives losing the allegory

concepts.title: The Padyāvalī Catalogue of Devotional Modes
concepts.description: nine exemplars with no ranking, *kapipati-dāsya* as authority exercised from inside servanthood, and the absent gopīs

concepts.title: The Deliberate Submission
concepts.description: the Brahmāstra accepted to preserve an institution and to buy an audience; the rope that nullifies it, and a false achievement transferred to Meghanāda

concepts.title: The Siddhis Are the Last Obstacle
concepts.description: the sun-Rāhu-Airāvata allegory, powers issued by the thing that stopped you, and the gaps where the decoding runs out

concepts.title: One Syllable
concepts.description: the Caṇḍī-yajña inverted by a single consonant; the boon refused first, the staff role chosen for access, and the ethical cost the volume files under wit

concepts.title: Silent Until Named
concepts.description: Kiṣkindhā 66's leap-distance auction as a format that selects on the wrong variable, and Jāmbavān reading the record back

concepts.title: Reading Epithets as Argument
concepts.description: the adjacency method, its constraint, and why an invocation built for repetition wants more surface than a text read once

concepts.title: Discernment as the Real Skill
concepts.description: virtue as calibration; the honest-obstacle criterion deciding which toolkit is available, and the converted obstacle that pays

concepts.title: Speed Bound to Restraint
concepts.description: every speed-epithet welded to a constraint, governed from within and aimed from without; the courier reading

concepts.title: Abode of Strength, Not Its Owner
concepts.description: *baladhāma* against *baladhan*; strength held in trust rather than owned, and what that changes for the person praying

concepts.title: No Fixed Form
concepts.description: cat, mosquito, thumb and Trivikrama in one episode; variance as the finding, and the one description from a witness inside the story

concepts.title: Two Accounts of the Invulnerability
concepts.description: the Mahākāla liṅga against a committee of six, in one treatise; a redundant list, and the harms nobody insured against

concepts.title: The Body Read as Function
concepts.description: biography converted into anatomy, arms against hands, and a closing claim that orientation outranks every capability catalogued

concepts.title: The Necklace Broken Tooth by Tooth
concepts.description: a queen's gift destroyed in public, the standard turned on his own body, and why it had to be pearls

concepts.title: The Prayer That Cooled the Fire
concepts.description: three conditionals a god cannot refuse; a prisoner's only instrument, and the same examiner who will test her later

concepts.title: Four Accounts of the Śiva-Sonship
concepts.description: a boon riding in the *putreṣṭi* offering, an involuntary loss through the ear, a layered possession giving two fathers, and a request with no conception in it; four mechanisms, no adjudication, and each one load-bearing for something different

concepts.title: Three Abodes at Once
concepts.description: Kimpuruṣavarṣa, the Himālaya and a transcendent Ayodhyā in the present tense together, defended by a figure who holds no territorial dominion; and in all three he is the resident rather than the reason

concepts.title: Who Taught Hanuman
concepts.description: Sūrya taught from a moving chariot, Rāma's *jñāna-mudrā* taught nothing and transmitted anyway, Kesarī taught before birth, Sītā taught the man sent to rescue her; four answers sorted by what each is needed for

concepts.title: The Inner Form
concepts.description: *bhāva-vigraha* as the shape the physical description is an interpretation of, *āptakāma* as fullness rather than restraint, and the devotee whose love overwhelmed perception instead of sharpening it

concepts.title: He Becomes the Weapon
concepts.description: no named instrument anywhere; trees, boulders, teeth and tail as interchangeable, availability displacing craftsmanship, and an instrument with a name understood as a possession

concepts.title: The Battle-Cry and Its Casualties
concepts.description: cosmological escalation that could have ended at Brahmā and ends instead on miscarriages indoors; printed twice from different texts by different contributors, and weighed by neither

concepts.title: The Chosen Form of Servant
concepts.description: an incarnation that could take any form choosing the servant's, a god with an appetite for the view from underneath, and the vanara body read as equipment selected rather than limitation accepted

concepts.title: The Boon of Never Being Satisfied
concepts.description: a request for permanent insufficiency with the length of stay arriving as its consequence, granted with an addition, and received in tears

concepts.title: Deflection: How He Handles Praise
concepts.description: branch-to-branch as transmitted technique rather than personality; praise named as a mechanism with an entry point, and affectionate praise identified as the dangerous case because scepticism is unavailable

concepts.title: The Catalogue of Singular Trust
concepts.description: seven assignments given to nobody else, four of them messages and none of them a battle; the courier's category, which the essay lists and does not name

concepts.title: The Sermon in the Enemy's Court
concepts.description: each clause landing on something Rāvaṇa specifically has; composure sufficient to tailor an argument while bound before an executioner, which is a stronger claim than the divinity the essay infers

concepts.title: Gati Read Three Ways
concepts.description: the root's second semantic field subdivided by the grammarians into knowledge, movement and attainment, and the one derivation in a long etymological essay that has a constraint and can fail

concepts.title: The Parents Read as Doctrine
concepts.description: *Añjaneya* and *Jānakī-śoka-nāśana* recurring together; an argument from collocation rather than from roots, and therefore falsifiable in a way the rest of the essay is not

concepts.title: Logic Has No Fixed Foundation
concepts.description: how the complete can want anything, asked and left unanswered on the *Brahma Sūtra*'s authority; a published rule invoked before the argument rather than after it fails

concepts.title: The Godāvarī Tīrtha and Vṛṣākapi
concepts.description: a bathing-place carrying four names, a *Brahma Purāṇa* etiology that assigns a person to each, and an identification of Vṛṣākapi with Hanuman resting on nothing but the shared riverbank ⚑ **flagged: the weak reasoning is named on the page and not repaired**, because it is an inference the essay makes in a subordinate clause and never examines

concepts.title: Every Relationship at Once
concepts.description: the Śṛṅgerī benediction reading the epic as a catalogue of the positions a person can occupy toward another; five relationships named where the claim is *every*, the concession that the attention moves off Rāma from the *Sundarkāṇḍa* onward, and a cardinal seat certifying a village cult it neither runs nor can regulate

concepts.title: The Apotropaic Register
concepts.description: three modern poems and one *dhyāna* verse folded into what the devotional poetry claims he *does for you*; a harm-list made entirely of ordinary bad years (ghosts, planets, dreams, poverty, disease) with no theological problem on it, three incompatible grammars for one promise, and the stanza that credits the telling rather than the god

title: Phase 1B — the extension corpus, archetypal-embodiment cluster (2026-08-14)

concepts.title: Identification Is the Tradition, Not the Departure
concepts.description: the corpus frames tantric identification with Hanuman as a Vajrayana graft onto a bhakti stock that has no such move; *vastutas tvam evāham* is the tradition's own summit claim, attested three times in the volume it cites, one of them by *Kalyāṇ*'s own editor. The cost of the mistake is not embarrassment but the **forfeited constraint** — Rāmsukhdās's criterion that service must continue undiminished, which is the behavioural test for inflation the corpus's protocol lacks

concepts.title: Three Stages Against Three Registers
concepts.description: the corpus builds a developmental ladder from the same three positions the *kastvam* verse holds simultaneously; the **instrumental case** (*dehadṛṣṭyā*, *jīvadṛṣṭyā*) settles it, since instruments coexist and stages do not. Plus a terminological finding checkable against the vault's own Gauḍīya corpus: `sādhana-bhakti` moved from first position to second and `bhāva-bhakti` installed at a summit that has at least seven degrees above it

concepts.title: Shadow Devotion Was Never Excluded
concepts.description: the Shadow-Devotion Paradox's premise that devotional paths avoid negative emotions, against Ramlal's seven registers with wrath as the seventh; a corrective built against an absent opponent inherits nothing, which is why the Dvārakā prohibition and the inward-redirection requirement went unfound rather than rejected

concepts.title: The Divine Wrath Practice and Its Missing Prohibitions
concepts.description: ⚠️ **flagged page, flag in the body at the top before any quotation reaches the reader.** A three-level arousal-amplifying protocol with genuinely good safety architecture — prerequisite gates, a referral clause, motive examination, de-escalation close — and two absent constraints available in the volume it cites. The finding is structural: **its trigger condition is evaluated by the faculty the practice amplifies**, where the tradition's prohibitions survive the state they govern

concepts.title: The Contemporary Divine Form
concepts.description: Iteration 18's instruction to visualise yourself in your own work environment rather than as traditionally depicted Hanuman, which quietly discards the iconographic form eight months of the corpus's own practice is built on. **The tradition supports it better than the corpus knows** — this is the one deity whose defining property is having no fixed form, with the guises organised by task. The extension is real and lies elsewhere than claimed: the tradition varies *his* form, the corpus varies *yours*, and the selection criterion goes missing in transit

concepts.title: The Recognition Signs Are Other People's Reports
concepts.description: the gates on a 36-month curriculum are set by what colleagues are said to notice; **the corpus's one named failure mode is spiritual materialism, and the recognition signs are item-for-item what an inflating practitioner would sincerely report** — the detector is built from the disease's symptoms. Thirteen documents contain no reports of anybody practising. Against the *Ānanda Rāmāyaṇa*'s eight fruits, which are first-person states and can come back empty

concepts.title: Two Incompatible Accounts of Anger
concepts.description: integrate it as sacred rage (Topic 3) or convert it away via Raudra→Śānta (months 3–4), in two documents that never meet and score the same behaviour opposite ways. **The curriculum trains minutes-to-dissipation and then gates a practice whose entire method is to sustain and amplify.** Plus: rasas are registers, not stages, and the same author reaches simultaneity — *"archetypal chords"* — in the rasa domain while imposing sequence in the bhakti one

concepts.title: Practice Risk Indexed to Body Type
concepts.description: the Vata/Pitta/Kapha adaptations, including the best safety instruction in the cluster (the tantric mantra rationed to weekly for three months for Pitta types, with a behavioural stop condition). **A real safety apparatus pointed at a proxy**: it asks whether you are Vata and never asks about the Bipolar II, BPD and epilepsy the same corpus documents. Dose-gates against the tradition's conduct-gates — complementary halves that each fail where the other holds — and the sleep-and-digestion indicators the corpus already owns and does not gate progression on

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta — Cluster K, The Madness of Separation, 2026-08-14 (COMPLETE, 17 pages)

concepts.title: Mādana and Mohana
concepts.description: the two divisions of the highest ecstasy with *udghūrṇā* and *citra-jalpa* beneath the second, and the line that makes the Antya-līlā legible; a taxonomy made only of relationship-states, which blocks trait inference by construction

concepts.title: Divya-unmāda
concepts.description: madness catalogued at the summit rather than as breakdown, inverting the surrounding yogic instruction; the category does not suspend the corpus's judgement of conduct but satisfies it in advance

concepts.title: Ardha-bāhya
concepts.description: the half-external state named by the corpus, which is the only condition in which absorption and speech coexist and therefore the channel the whole book came through; a bandwidth that passes formula, affect and repetition

concepts.title: The Body That Changes Shape
concepts.description: elongation and tortoise-retraction as opposite deformations under one cause, three chapters apart, never connected by any layer; written as measurement in a text that otherwise never measures

concepts.title: The Fisherman and the Ghost
concepts.description: the only witness who had not been told: accurate description, demonic diagnosis, and a failure to recognise him; independent in content and dependent in transmission

concepts.title: Vṛndāvana Overwrites Purī
concepts.description: the narrator's own generalisation with three acted-on instances; a prior that has reached the identification step, where *look again* is the compromised operation

concepts.title: The Yogi of My Mind
concepts.description: the mind as a mendicant with the ten senses as disciples, itemised object by object; externalising past the point where it stops being a technique and becomes a report that nobody is home

concepts.title: The Five Senses on One Horse
concepts.description: the standard sense-control prescription quoted and declined because the pull is a fact about the object; and it is the senses of perception, not action, that tear the horse apart

concepts.title: The Person I Want to Forget Is Lying in My Heart
concepts.description: the resolution to stop is the summoning; ironic-process theory four centuries early, described accurately and attributed to the object for want of a comparison case

concepts.title: Condemning Providence
concepts.description: system, beloved, self, in one speech with nothing learned in between; and defamation catalogued as a permitted devotional register rather than excused as a lapse

concepts.title: Rubbing His Face on the Walls
concepts.description: self-injury read as transport by the household and explained by him as a failed search for a door; expression is the residual category, and somebody asked

concepts.title: Advaita's Equivocal Sonnet
concepts.description: a coded message acknowledged in three words and then publicly disclaimed; deniability among allies, where its function is relieving the room of the obligation to respond

concepts.title: The Flute as Yoginī Messenger
concepts.description: the transgression engineered and then lectured about, with the instruction named as the injury; an accurate diagnosis delivered to the operator that changes nothing

concepts.title: Citra-jalpa and the Bumblebee Song
concepts.description: ten divisions of deranged speech with the bumblebee song as worked example, plus the vocabulary for affect arriving, meeting and colliding; a community that classifies has stopped diagnosing

concepts.title: The Vision That Analyses Itself
concepts.description: rhetorical figures named mid-vision; the apparent counter-example to the transmission constraint, resolving once the analysis is seen as recognition rather than construction

concepts.title: The Woman on His Shoulder
concepts.description: a foot on the shoulder, the servant rebuked, and a request for her blessing; eagerness as the credential, and the one place that uninspectable criterion left a trace

concepts.title: Interrogating the Trees
concepts.description: silence from masculine trees read as loyalty and from feminine creepers as fear; a prior needs no input to produce output, and absence is the most permissive input there is

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta — Cluster L, The Śikṣāṣṭaka, 2026-08-14 (COMPLETE, 6 pages)

concepts.title: The Śikṣāṣṭaka
concepts.description: the only composition Caitanya left, containing no theology, no instruction and no identity claim, placed last as the corpus's authenticity anchor; and a disclosure clause making every failure to understand a fact about the reader

concepts.title: Tṛṇād api Sunīcena
concepts.description: lower than the grass, tolerant as a tree, with the gloss on what a tree's tolerance means; produced and achieved self-abnegation are behaviourally identical and only the surroundings separate them

concepts.title: Āśliṣya vā Pāda-ratāṁ
concepts.description: a commitment with no exit condition that ranks abandonment above harm; the interior state is identical whether or not anybody is on the other end, and the holder has no access to the difference

concepts.title: Rādhā's Monologue on the Rival
concepts.description: ⚠️ flagged page, flag in the body at the top. The procured rival, the condemnation of one's own anger, the leper's wife; and Madhya 8 makes that same anger the engine of the rāsa-līlā

concepts.title: Na Dhanaṁ Na Janaṁ
concepts.description: four refusals of which only the fourth was live for the man composing; *ahaitukī* devotion, and why a motive that can never be satisfied is indistinguishable from one that is not a lack

concepts.title: Service Sweeter Than Union
concepts.description: Lakṣmī on the chest wanting the feet; union is a state and service is an activity, and only one has a gradient, which is why arrival is this tradition's standing complaint

title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta — Cluster M, The Book About Its Own Making, 2026-08-14 (COMPLETE, 4 pages)

concepts.title: The Disclaimed Author
concepts.description: three authors across four centuries disclaiming authorship in one grammatical move with its stock image attached, and the corpus's own diagnosis of the device as a characteristic of advanced devotees

concepts.title: The Author Believes It Anyway
concepts.description: no corroboration, no scriptural support, generally disbelieved, one named eyewitness, and belief asserted anyway; candour and accuracy are independent properties and this passage is where they come apart

concepts.title: Blasphemy as Prayer
concepts.description: defamation catalogued among six recognised ecstatic modes, with a stated consequence and an attempted repair; a written permission running upward in its target and downward in its availability

concepts.title: The Sequel's Self-Positioning
concepts.description: exalt the predecessor, define yourself by his gaps, defer finality to a Vyāsadeva who will not arrive; three moves that make a work subordinate, necessary and non-final, and why this canon can never close

concepts.title: Adaptive Scaling and the Siddhis
concepts.description: the corpus's five-rung consciousness-scale ladder (atomic, individual, community, cosmic, adaptive) against the four size-*siddhis* Pāṭhak maps one-to-one onto episodes. **The tradition's version is the more usable and that is not the expected result**: *aṇimā* and *mahimā* are opposites rather than rungs, and they are indexed to *problems* rather than to scope — a mosquito to defeat detection, a small form to establish credibility with a frightened captive, a mountain form to answer a challenge that scales. **A ladder tells you where you are; a mapping tells you what to do.** ⚠ The one clinically-shaped application, *shrinking consciousness size when situations become too complex*, inverts every instance in the volume, where shrinking is instrumental and outward-facing rather than relief from overwhelm

title: Phase 2 — Aṅka, Envoy Sage & Scripture (14 essays, read in full, saturated at Pass 5). Batch 1, 2026-08-14

concepts.title: Four Standards for One Envoy
concepts.description: four contributors set out what an envoy must be and **not one cites the same source as any other**: Caturvedī's eleven-item checklist attributed to nothing, Miśra's single dramatic-theory category, Lakṣmaṇ Śāstrī's five-part Agni Purāṇa definition with no chapter or verse, and Draviḍ's Arthaśāstra maxim with no book, chapter or mention of Kauṭilya. ⚑ **The statecraft cluster is sourced markedly worse than the theology beside it** — Draviḍ quotes Vālmīki 6.18.33 exactly in the same short essay where he leaves the Arthaśāstra bare, so the precision was available and was not spent. **Each contributor's standard tracks his own discipline rather than the evidence.** What survives intersecting the four is two requirements — exact memory and composure under pressure — arrived at independently, which is the one place the volume's convening method produces evidence rather than noise. And **all four pass Hanuman on every criterion they set**, which makes them portraits rather than tests

concepts.title: The Verses Never Overlap
concepts.description: four *Mantra-Rāmāyaṇa* readers hunting Hanuman in the Ṛgveda, and **zero verses appear on two lists**. Gaṅgeśvarānand takes RV 1.1.1, 4.18.9, 2.35 and 10.30; Rāmkumārdās takes 10.28.8–10, 10.53.7, 10.87.1/2/6/22 and 9.72.1; Ramlal gives **no verse numbers at all**; Nīlakaṇṭha, already built, gives 9.73.7 and 10.64.8. ⚑ **Nīlakaṇṭha is cited as the authority by two of them and yields two different verse-sets.** The same disjointness recurs on the praṇava — three mutually independent derivations in one group — which takes it to `[n≥3 PATTERN]`. Two licences make it possible and **neither has an off-switch**: "the gods love the indirect" (attributed to the Aitareya by one contributor and the Bṛhadāraṇyaka by another, neither with a verse) and the Padma Purāṇa Śeṣa-nāga permission for partial telling, **which predicts exactly this pattern and thereby forfeits agreement as evidence**. ⚑ **The only caveat anywhere is the modern renderer's**, not the volume's

concepts.title: Two Licences With No Off-Switch
concepts.description: *"the gods love the indirect"* (attributed to the Aitareya by one contributor and the Bṛhadāraṇyaka by another, neither with a verse) and the Padma Purāṇa **Śeṣa-nāga permission** that everyone tells only as much as their understanding allows. **Neither specifies a case where it does not apply**, which is what separates them from *arthavāda*, whose external-contradiction requirement can fail to obtain, and from kalpa-plurality, whose mixing-prohibition constrains it. ⚑ **The Śeṣa-nāga permission predicts the very non-convergence that would otherwise disconfirm the Vedic readings** — and a doctrine that explains away disagreement has forfeited agreement as evidence. They remain strong as *testimony about the tradition* and empty as *warrant for a reading*, and the volume uses them as the second

concepts.title: Simvaran and the Symptom That Can Be Absent
concepts.description: the Rāmsnehī sampradāya's graded name-repetition: *adham* at the tongue with a sweetness like crystallised sugar, *madhyam* at the throat with a humming, *uttam* at the heart with a drumming *dham-dhamkār*, *ati-uttam* at the navel with the syllable *ra* resonating. ★ **Every rung names something that can fail to appear** — which is exactly the property the extension corpus's Recognition Signs lack, supplied four hundred pages away in the same volume and in the same idiom. **Hanuman identified with *prāṇa* itself**, embodying the restlessness he then settles: the deity who *is* the instability is the model for mastering it, which is why this sampradāya makes him central to a *japa* practice specifically

concepts.title: A Norm Inferred From One Compliance
concepts.description: Hanuman stops fighting and claims that **as an envoy he cannot lawfully be killed**; Meghanāda captures rather than kills; and Lakṣmaṇ Śāstrī treats the compliance as validating the norm. **No text is cited anywhere.** ⚑ Compliance is only evidence of a norm when the complier had reason to prefer defection, and Meghanāda had every reason to want him alive — and if the submission was staged, as three other accounts in this volume hold, **the compliance was procured and cannot evidence anything**

concepts.title: Admitting the Defector
concepts.description: the Vibhīṣaṇa council, worked by two contributors who agree on the verdict and disagree completely about what kind of question it was: Draviḍ argues from **Rāma's vow at Vālmīki 6.18.33**, a pre-commitment that removes the discretion, and Pañcariā argues from incentives and information. ⚑ **Nobody answers Sugrīva.** His objection was that Vibhīṣaṇa is the kind of person who leaves; the four counters establish only that he is not a plant — and the epic then bears Sugrīva out, since Vibhīṣaṇa does exactly what was predicted. **The disloyalty that makes a defector suspect is the same disposition that makes him valuable**

concepts.title: The Devotee Who Asks the Questions
concepts.description: the Upaniṣadic Hanuman across three texts and three incompatible postures: questioner in the Muktikā, authority in the Rāma Rahasya answering Sanaka and Prahlāda, silent listener in the *Rāma-pūrvottara-tāpanīya*'s yantra, placed inside the triangle with Śatrughna and Bharata. **A dialogue's form makes him the condition of the doctrine's existence**, which is a strong claim arriving by literary structure rather than by assertion. The answer his questions produce is **a reading list** — 1,180 branches, a progression to 108 — which presupposes a canon too large to read

concepts.title: A Gāyatrī for a Devotee
concepts.description: seven pages on *oṃ rāmadūtāya vidmahe kapirājāya dhīmahi, tanno hanumān pracodayāt*, read as jñāna/dhyāna/samarpaṇa with **the plural *us* as ego-dissolution**, and **no defence anywhere of whether a deity-Gāyatrī is legitimate** — the live objection, given that the Gāyatrī is Ṛgveda 3.62.10 addressed to Savitṛ. ⚑ **The three-stage structure is a property of the template, not of this mantra.** ⚑ **The apparatus is tantric and the form claimed is Vedic**: the *devatā* designation comes from the *Kulārṇava Tantra*, and *ṛṣi/chandas/devatā* is the Vedic *viniyoga* formula. Three versions circulate and one is analysed; no prerequisites, eligibility, count, timing or method

title: Phase 3 — the extension corpus, strategy/statecraft cluster (16 documents, read in full, saturated at Pass 5). Batch 1, 2026-08-14

concepts.title: Sītā's Ordeal as a Self-Worth Exercise
concepts.description: ⚠️ **FLAGGED PAGE, flag in the body at the top.** Two guided visualisations recast **Sītā's trial by fire** as an exercise for clearing self-doubt (*"step into the flames with complete willingness to be tested"*, emerging *"verified"* with *"certification of your true purity"*) and **her abduction** as a model for a bad job (*"your 'Lanka' — the place where you feel held against your will"*). **Both reframes delete the party whose conduct produced the situation** — the accuser relocated into the self, the captor into circumstance — and the deletion is required by the technique rather than incidental to it. ⚑ **The corpus inherits an interpretation without marking it as one**: its practice runs entirely on *fire reveals what is true*, which is the reading every contributor in the volume supplies, while this build's `the-prayer-that-cooled-the-fire` found the speech to be **skilled advocacy** — three conditionals a god cannot refuse. *A practice built on a text inherits that text's reception, not the text.* ⚠ Across the fifteen figure-practices the **male figures get doing and the female figure gets withstanding** (Rāma: agency; Hanuman: capability; Sītā: endurance), bounded as a claim about these fifteen as written. And the corpus's risk model has **exactly one dimension, arousal** — which is why the wrath practices got gates and a protocol training *willingness to be tested* got none. The page takes no position on whether the *agni-parīkṣā* is vindication or injustice

concepts.title: The Warrior-Sage Who Is Not a Kṣatriya
concepts.description: the strategy framework names **Warrior-Sage (*kṣatriya-ṛṣi*)** as its governing archetype and never revisits the choice. ⚑ **Hanuman is not inside varṇa on any of the volume's three incompatible readings** — a twice-born parallel civilisation, *animals by birth* said by himself, or a form taken up and set down — and *kṣatriya* is not a synonym for warrior but a birth-rank with entailed authority. **A kṣatriya's problem is what to do with authority he already has; Hanuman's is capability with no standing whatsoever**, which is the position the framework's reader is actually in and the source of every distinctive move in the corpus. The volume's own reading is that the low form was **chosen to remove status**, so the compound runs backwards. ⚠ The **Golden Mountain Principle** repeats the move — three stability terms asserted of the figure most insisted to have no fixed form — and *niśṛṣṭārtha dūta*, a status-free operational role with its own named limit, sits unused in the same build. Also: *vīrya* listed as a third track beside *buddhi* and *jñāna* is a category error, and the Warrior Strategy track is correspondingly the one with the least distinctive content

concepts.title: The Devotional Supercomputer
concepts.description: the nervous system visualised as hardware, *install Hanuman software*, *"fiber-optic cables of golden light"*, surrender rendered as releasing processing load. **The third borrowed technical vocabulary** after quantum entanglement and standing waves. ⚑ **Run the deletion test and this one splits, which the previous two did not**: *install* → *take on the disposition* loses nothing, *fibre-optic cables* → *channels of golden light* loses nothing, but **release your processing** is a **scoped, partial, reversible surrender** — a division of labour with a boundary — and *prapatti* is by definition unbounded and total. The corpus has arrived at a bounded surrender without knowing it departed from anything, and for a reader with a working week to run the bounded version is the usable one. **Three bins, not two: misuse, decoration, earned metaphor** — the corpus has one of each. ⚠ The risk is in *install*, which replaces a timescale with an event, against a volume whose whole account is proximity and duration. And the naming is countable: of five Hanuman practices, the two named for machines are the two with no episode behind them

title: Phase 4 — Aṅka, Character & Virtue (21 essays, read in full BEFORE writing, saturated at Pass 5). Batch 1, 2026-08-14

concepts.title: The Four-Axis Service Framework
concepts.description: Mukundpati Tripāṭhī names four requirements and reads the whole career as their execution: **intelligence to act · discernment to judge · strength to carry through · timing sharp enough to know exactly when to move** — drawn, he says, from **Rāma's own instructions to Lakṣmaṇa about guarding Sītā**, which makes the framework *derived* rather than composed and explains why the number is an awkward four. ⚑ **Timing is not a capacity but a relation between a capacity and a moment**, so the framework is three capacities and one thing governing when they are spent. Two instances, both **anticipatory**: lighting the alliance-fire the moment an opening appears, and pre-empting Rāma's anger over Sugrīva's forgetting. ⚠ **The herb-mountain episode skips the discernment axis entirely** — he takes the whole mountain *"without wasting a moment weighing his options"*, and the essay approves — which yields the precedence rule the volume left out: **when the axes conflict, timing wins, because it is the only one whose window closes.** Set against a seventeen-item virtue catalogue in the same group, and against a modern strategy cluster with three tracks and no timing term at all

concepts.title: The Rescue He Deliberately Did Not Make
concepts.description: Kumbhakarṇa carries an unconscious Sugrīva off; Hanuman closes the distance easily **and does not intervene**, because a king retrieved by his own minister returns **indebted for his own freedom** and diminished as a warrior. ⚑ **The reasoning is unspeakable, not merely unspoken** — it cannot be said to its beneficiary without undoing itself — so the act only works if nobody ever learns why. **Non-action is not restraint**: restraint uses less force and still delivers the outcome; this accepts a materially worse world on purpose, and from outside is indistinguishable from cowardice or inattention. ⚑ **Third instance of one shape**, with the Aṅgada inversion — his own comrade denies he burned Laṅkā at all, reasoning that a man who had would have come forward — and Rāvaṇa's spies filing him as *"the weakest monkey in the entire army."* **Self-effacement does not merely go unrewarded; it destroys the record of the act, in ally and enemy intelligence alike**

concepts.title: The Invocation Order Shifts
concepts.description: ⭐ **the most checkable argument found in six hundred pages of this volume.** Jayarāmdās "Dīn" Rāmāyaṇī claims the *Mānas* encodes the Hanuman-as-Śiva identification in the order of its own opening verses: **Śiva's invocation precedes Rāma's through Araṇya Kāṇḍa; from Kiṣkindhā onward the order reverses** *"in keeping with a servant's proper humility"*; **and in Sundarkāṇḍa Hanuman's invocation occupies Śiva's traditional position entirely.** Grounded on *Dohāvalī* 142–143. ⚑ **Unlike the volume's etymologies (five held at once), its Vedic identifications (four disjoint verse-sets) and its allegories (licensed by *arthavāda*), this one can come out false and anybody could establish that.** ⚠ **Recorded as the essay's claim only — this build has not opened a *Mānas*** — and the essay supplies **no verse numbers and no edition**, which is the whole gap between a good argument and a finished one. `[n=1 CHANGEPOINT]`: one boundary across seven books, at a location the doctrine predicts

concepts.title: The Eightfold Brahmacarya
concepts.description: *naiṣṭhik brahmacarya* given a technical definition from the **Dakṣa Saṃhitā** as **eight violations**: thinking about a woman with desire · describing her beauty · flirting · gazing with desire · speaking privately from desire · wanting her · intending union · the act. ⚑ **The first is a gaze, which converts the harem search from a mild puzzle into a genuine crisis** — refusing to look makes the search impossible, and there is no third option. The resolution is doctrinal: **intention determines merit, not the act**. ⚠ **But every article carries a desire-clause, so the enumeration promised a checkable standard and the doctrine relocates all eight back inside the practitioner.** Also **Bhartṛhari's warrant for the title *Mahāvīr*** — breaking the pride of desire, not splitting an elephant's skull — **Kālidāsa's *dhīra*** requiring temptation to be fully present, the **consortless incarnation** offered as evidence for the Mahārudra identification, vanara polygamy making the celibacy a deliberate exception to his own society, and **Gandhi's years of failed method** concluding devotion rather than willpower. 🔴 Carries one of the volume's two conceded lapses

concepts.title: The Two Lapses the Volume Concedes
concepts.description: 🔴 **exactly two moments in twenty-one essays where a contributor states that something went wrong inside the figure.** S. N. Pāṇḍey: struck by **Bharata's arrow** while carrying the Sañjīvanī mountain and offered passage on Bharata's own arrows, pride flickers — ***"how could any arrow bear my own weight?"*** — and dissolves **within a single breath**. Rāmamādhav Ciṅgle: in Rāvaṇa's chambers his mind ***"genuinely wavered, if only briefly."*** ⚑ **Both are conceded by the contributor with the strictest standard in play, and that is a mechanism rather than a coincidence: a standard specified finely enough to be failed makes failures visible.** ⚑ **Pāṇḍey then converts the admission into the measurement** — humility as a **recovery rate** rather than a state, which *requires* the lapse and cannot be evidenced without it. ⚠ **The limit is exact: the volume admits imperfect interiority and never admits a mistaken decision.** Against five essays insisting on perfect composure, one quoting Vālmīki 5.11.41–42. Plus **three incompatible reasons for the post-Laṅkā silence** — rank protocol, moral unease, and fear as Aṅgada misreads it

concepts.title: Pratyabhijñā Run Backwards
concepts.description: Śrīnivāsācārya names ***pratyabhijñā-śakti*** as Hanuman's defining faculty and glosses *buddhimatāṃ variṣṭham* as naming it — but uses it **transitively**, for perceiving other people, where the Śaiva term is **reflexive**, meaning recognition of one's own identity with Śiva. ⚑ **And the volume, across three essays, credits him with the transitive power in its highest form while denying him the reflexive one in its most basic** — Jāmbavān asking why one of such capacity **lacks self-recognition**, and the curse leaving him unable to recall his own strength until told. **A term meaning self-recognition, applied to a figure defined by its absence.** ⚑ **The essay's better half is its opening**: gods and sages routinely fail to recognise holiness — **Indra astonished that a demon could pray, Durvāsas ruined by misreading Ambarīṣa** — which makes recognition-*failure* the real subject and locates it in the observer's category overriding the evidence in front of them. 🔴 Vibhīṣaṇa's epistemics split the volume: immediate recognition here, an explicit evidentiary threshold in Rāmāyaṇī. `[RENDERING — verify against Hindi]`

concepts.title: The Boundary on the Name
concepts.description: ⭐ **Rāma's name is not for ordinary worldly requests — it is reserved for liberation alone — and for everyday troubles one should call on Hanuman instead**, he *"keeping the largest name in reserve, and taking the rest of the burden on himself."* ⚑ **A division of petitionary labour that sorts by a property of the request rather than of the petitioner**, protects the higher term by restricting access to it, and has the intermediary **absorb** rather than relay. ⚑⚑ **This is the theological warrant `the-apotropaic-register` recorded as missing** — it explains at once why the harms are ordinary, why the promises attach to Hanuman, and why the cluster looked unfounded: **its warrant sits a hundred and fifty pages away, in a different group, in a closing paragraph.** ⚠ **Which upgrades a standing finding: the files-its-answer-away-from-its-question pattern is not a property of the amateur modern corpus at all — it occurs here in the most professionally edited artefact in this build, and is a property of any multi-author corpus.** Cost the essay never counts: a devotee told not to bring their ordinary life to their highest devotion. ⚑ **UPDATED 2026-08-15 — the claim splits in two.** The ***Devotion to Rāma*** group attests the **intermediary function** four more times, in four registers — an **office** (Karpātrī), a positive route (*tumhare bhajana rāma ko pāvai*, Śarmā), the Bharata-character parallel (Siṅh), and a **gate**: *"Hanuman guards Rāma's own door, and no one enters that court without his permission first"* (Seṭh) — and attests the **reservation of the Name** not once. 🚩 **SINGLE SOURCE stands on the restriction and is removed from the function.** 🔴 **And the group's name-material runs the other way** — a name that saves all three worlds daily, outweighs *jñāna* and *dhyāna* combined, and waives every prerequisite. ⚑ **The motive arrives too**, from Premnidhi: *"a jealous kind of grace"*, permanently
