watchful, worship manuals instructing devotees to **please Hanuman fully first** — *"not as formality"* but from **protectiveness over how Rāma's attention gets spent, with wounded feelings when bypassed.** Neither humility nor self-establishment, and the only one of the three the volume states

concepts.title: Bajrangbali as a Translation
concepts.description: Revāprasād Dvivedī claims **Bajrangbali** and **Vajraṅgavīr** are vernacular renderings of ***vajra-saṃhanana***, the fourth item in **Yoga Sūtra Vibhūti Pāda 46**'s *kāya-sampat* — which would make the commonest devotional name in northern India a translation of a technical term in a yoga manual. ⚑ **Vācaspati glosses it as a body whose parts are *"as densely knit as a thunderbolt"* — jointure, not hardness** — which fits a shape-shifter far better than invulnerability does, and matches the volume's own inconsistency about his protection. ⚠ **The rival derivation is stated rather than suppressed**: *vajra-aṅga*, thunderbolt-limbed, is the standard account, and this build has not adjudicated. The **exclusivity claim** — that these epithets attach to no other deity — is what would convert resemblance into descent, and is asserted without a survey. Plus three further siddhi mappings, each pairing chapter-and-verse to a numbered sūtra through a named commentator. 🔴 The body as attained *kāya-sampat* against Ramlal's body as issued equipment. `[RENDERING — verify against Hindi]`

concepts.title: Three Answers to the Archetype Question
concepts.description: the volume's positive reply to the modern framework's *kṣatriya-ṛṣi*. **Akhaṇḍānand**: a human servant beside a human Rāma would invite comparison *"in caste, appearance, qualities, diet, and living manner"*, so **the vanara form was selected to remove the grounds of comparison** — four of those five markers being the ordinary furniture of caste. **Avasthī**: he holds **all four varṇa-strengths simultaneously** — priest's disciplined, warrior's martial, merchant's providing, labourer's serving — which makes naming him by two of the four a subtraction rather than a compression. **Śukratna**: **Samarth Rāmdās established two images, *Dās Māruti* and *Vīr Māruti*** — servitude and heroism **instantiated separately rather than fused**, with *"whoever can genuinely be a servant is the only one who ever really gets to be a hero"* ordering them. ⚑ **Three incompatible arguments, one shared refusal to name a rank** — `[n=3]`, and the volume supplies counter-instances (Puruṣottama, the eleventh Rudra). Akhaṇḍānand argues celibacy and even ugliness the same functional way

concepts.title: The Offer That Was Staged
concepts.description: Hanuman offers to trample and tear apart the rākṣasī women who guarded Sītā, and Akhaṇḍānand alone names the anomaly: ***"a performance oddly out of character for him… and reads it as deliberate"*** — staged **to make Sītā's greatness visible, not his own.** Her reply invokes universal fault, **names her own wrongdoing against Lakṣmaṇa**, and grounds mercy in station rather than sentiment. ⭐ **The rule extracted from it is the most usable sentence in the group**: ***"does this action increase Rāma's own glory, or that of his devotees? If a decision fails that test, one's own devotion must be judged incomplete."*** ⚑ **An act-test, with a plural beneficiary, and a stated consequence — all three of which the modern corpus's own "Rāma Test" lacks**, and the corpus named its filter after Rāma without ever consulting the volume in which a better one already existed. Paired with **Sītā's refusal of transport**, protecting the form of the rescue at the cost of more captivity. 🔴 The staged reading is preserved against the plainer one — that the offer was genuine — and this page adopts neither, noting that the staged reading conveniently spares him the impulse

title: Phase 4 — Aṅka, Character & Virtue. Batch 2, 2026-08-14. **Group's candidate list exhausted.**

concepts.title: Svayamprabhā as Prātibha
concepts.description: Revāprasād Dvivedī identifies **a character with a siddhi**: Svayamprabhā of the Ṛkṣabila cave, *"self-luminous"*, matched to Patañjali's ***prātibha*** — *"a flash of intuitive insight"*, which **Vyāsa likens to the first glow of dawn before actual sunrise.** ⚠ **The name has a sufficient ordinary explanation** — it is what you would call a radiant being in a dark cave — and a name the setting already accounts for is not evidence for anything further. ⚑ **But the episode supports the reading better than the etymology does, and Dvivedī leads with the etymology**: she brings the vanaras out **only after telling them to close their eyes**, which stages knowledge-without-sensing at exactly the point where searching has failed. **Criterion proposed: an allegorical reading earns its place when it explains something the plain reading leaves unexplained** — on which three of the essay's four mappings pass and this one passes only on the ground its author did not use

concepts.title: Four Sampradāyas Agree on Dāsya
concepts.description: **Nārada, Rāmānuja, Madhva and Tulsīdās** convened to establish *dāsya-bhakti* as *"not a lesser form of love for God but the truest one."* ⚠ **They do not agree so much as fail to conflict**: three are making **ontological** claims about what a soul is, one is making a **practical** one, and the shared conclusion needs a premise none supplies. ⚑ **The envoy cluster is the control** — same volume, same convening method, **four unshared standards** — and the explanation is that *dāsya* is a question every Vaiṣṇava school was **constituted to answer** while envoy theory is not: *convergence among traditions is evidence about the subject only where the traditions were built to have positions on it.* ⚑ **The *ananya* verse converts *dāsya* from a relation with one person into a relation with everything** — *maĩ sevaka sacarācara rūpa svāmi bhagavanta* — with **Bhāgavata 8.7.44** making **grief at the world's suffering** the highest worship. `[n=4, NOT INDEPENDENT]`

concepts.title: The Four Roars
concepts.description: Jagdīś Śukla grades the Aśoka-vāṭikā fight by roar: **ordinary guards, no roar at all** · named warriors, an ordinary roar · Akṣa, the loud roar of battle-excitement · Meghanāda, gnashed teeth and a dead sprint. ⚑ **Four properties no instrument in the modern corpus has: ordinal with named anchors, third-party observable, involuntary, and able to return zero** — and it returns zero in the tier where the most killing happens, which separates exertion from engagement. ⚠ **It measures arousal, not threat**, and saturates at Meghanāda, who then defeats him. Plus **three strike-modes with the fist deadliest**, and **Kumbhakarṇa as a control**: *"what an entire army's mountain-hurling couldn't accomplish, one punch does immediately."* 🚩 SINGLE SOURCE

concepts.title: Three Ordeals, Three Guṇas
concepts.description: **Gītā 14.18 laid over the three sea-obstacles by vertical position** — Surasā in the air sāttvika, Laṅkinī at the gate rājasika, Siṃhikā below the waters tāmasika — which is a structural match rather than a resemblance. **Three opposite procedures**: out-grow the sāttvika and never fight it; destroy the tāmasika the instant it is recognised, *"never let even its shadow linger"*; and ⚑ **spare the rājasika — beaten half-senseless and deliberately left alive — because *rājasika tendencies cannot be eliminated without leaving the seeker without means of survival.*** **The volume's strongest allegory: it explains the one genuinely odd thing about the crossing, that a consistent figure used three incompatible methods in one sequence.** ⚠ Laṅkinī then **blesses him**, which the allegory has no room for; and the scheme needs a classifier it does not contain. 🔴 Against Prabhudatt Brahmacārī's version, same responses, no obstacle assignments. ⚑ **UPDATED 2026-08-15 — `[n=4 READ; 3 AGREEING; 1 UNASSIGNED]`.** Dvivedī and Śrīvāstava, both in the ***Devotion to Rāma*** group, assign the three **identically to Rāmāyaṇī's** with no cross-reference; Dvivedī adds the reading of all three as ***māyā in feminine disguise***, and Śrīvāstava supplies **the tamas classifier the scheme lacked** — Siṃhikā **seizes the shadow and corrupts the mind before the body falls**, so the defence is instant recognition — plus a sattva rule with teeth (*complete the task, then submit*) and the crispest rajas formulation (*strike hard enough to humble, never erase*). ⚠ **This puts the PRD's *"three incompatible mappings"* in doubt**: three read, three agreeing, source of the claim unidentified. **Flagged, not asserted**

concepts.title: The Brahmāstra: Two Explanations
concepts.description: 🔴 both contributors agree the submission was voluntary and give incompatible motives. **Goyandkā**: he lets the astra take him **calculating that capture buys an audience with Rāvaṇa**, then lets the rākṣasas add ordinary rope — **which voids the astra's hold** — and **keeps up the pretence of being restrained.** **Śukla**: he goes still *"out of respect for the weapon itself… a courtesy, not a defeat."* ⚑ **The rope is the discriminator: a person honouring a weapon does not exploit a loophole in it** — and Goyandkā's version stakes a checkable mechanical claim while Śukla's attributes a motive with nothing attached. ⚠ Four essays support a premeditating figure; one has him **uneasy at having burned Laṅkā without explicit prior order.** ⚑ And the live edge: propriety toward the astra and deception toward the captors may be different obligations, which would let both readings stand

concepts.title: The Mission Beyond the Message
concepts.description: Akhaṇḍānand **audits what the reconnaissance actually produced** and lists four things, **none of which is *found Sītā***: destroyed the military apparatus, **exposed Brahmāstra knowledge**, threw the administration into fear, unsettled soldier morale — with the logic that **if one scout did this, the enemy must scale what an army will do.** ⚑ **The mission's chief product was a belief installed in the enemy, not intelligence brought home**, which inverts what a scouting mission is for. ⚑ **The confidentiality doctrine**: nobody knew Rāma's actual message, because disclosure *"would have discouraged the other vanaras"* — a subordinate withholding, unauthorised, an accurate picture of his commander's state. Paired with **memory and discretion named together** in the closing formula. 🔴 **Against Jāmbavān, who states the envoy's limits before the crossing** — forbidden to initiate war, speaks only his master's intention — **with a self-defence carve-out.** The volume prints both and never puts them together

concepts.title: Testimony Sorted by Source
concepts.description: Śaṅkarānand Sarasvatī **states his evidentiary method before applying it**: *"the best evidence comes from what that person says of himself, from contemporaries who knew him, and — most tellingly — from what even his opponents are forced to admit."* **Three tiers ranked by interest**, with **Rāvaṇa's admission to his own generals** — having seen both Vālī and Sugrīva — as the top instance, delivered where flattery would be worse than useless. ⚑ **And the volume breaks it**: Rāvaṇa's **spies file him as *"the weakest monkey in the entire army."*** Same witness, same interest, opposite reports. **The scheme grades the witness by interest and never by access** — and against a subject managing his own appearance the adversary is the *most* manipulable, not the least. ⚠ The essay contains **no counter-argument of any kind**: an adversary's admission is still an adversary used affirmatively. **The missing fourth tier — conduct rather than testimony — exists in the volume, in a different essay**

concepts.title: The Weapon That Is a Summons
concepts.description: Kṛṣṇagopāl Māthur goes **outside the Rāmāyaṇa's timeline** and returns with the ***Kapīndrāstra*** of the ***Garga Saṃhitā*'s Viśvajit-khaṇḍa** — an astra invoked by **Kṛṣṇa's son** against the demon Kalaṅka, **whose effect is that Hanuman arrives in person.** ⚑ **An astra is owned and discharged; this one's effect is not under the invoker's control after the call — which makes it a summons filed under weapons, and names the mechanism the whole apotropaic apparatus runs on: you do not wield him, you call him and he decides.** ⚠ **At Pātāla he takes a goddess's seat in Ahirāvaṇa's rite and consumes her offerings** — extraordinary for a figure elsewhere defined by refusing position, and the volume prints it without comment. **The *Bhīṣma Parva*'s *Kapidhvaja* and *Kapiniketan*, surviving as Arjuna's own epithets, are the essay's strongest evidence and are not about Hanuman's deeds at all.** 🚩 SINGLE SOURCE throughout

concepts.title: Contributors Who Mark Their Own Register
concepts.description: **two of twenty-one contributors state what kind of thing they are writing.** Rāmnārāyaṇdatt Śāstrī declares his five *kavitta* verses ***"not scripture but a modern devotional retelling"***; Mukundpati Tripāṭhī marks his closing as ***"less an argument at that point than an admission."*** ⚑ **A marker forfeits borrowed standing — an unmarked poem printed between chapter-and-verse essays inherits their register by proximity alone** — which is why almost nobody does it, and why the ones who do are the ones worth trusting elsewhere. ⚑ **Muni Vidyānand, a Jain monastic using *vitarāga*, is placed in the *Character & Virtue* group rather than the comparative section**: the volume's pan-sectarian convening happens in the body, and an outside voice filed as testimony rather than coverage is what produces contradictions this deep. ⚠ **A third layer of caution belongs to the modern renderer, not the volume — the *Aṅka* is less hedged than it reads in English.** ⚑ **UPDATED 2026-08-15 — and the rate is a property of the group, not the volume.** ***Devotion to Rāma*** yields **three markings in sixteen essays** against two in twenty-one — a fourfold difference. **Rāmsukhdās marks a *doctrine* rather than a genre** (*parakīyā* as *"a spiritual ideal, not a literal model for conduct"*), **Premnidhi marks his scope** (colloquial devotion against devotion *"at its actual limit"*), and **Dvivedī marks his genealogy as *literal*** — *"not a figure of speech, on this reading"* — **a marker that raises the register instead of lowering it, and thereby accepts refutability.** ⚑ **The better-cited group is the one that marks**: contributors who cite have thought about what kind of claim they are making. ⚠ Extraction log tallies five; **three carry an attributed contributor and a quoted phrase and three is what is claimed**

concepts.title: The Four Ratis and the Inversion
concepts.description: Svāmī Rāmsukhdās, *Kalyāṇ*'s own editor, names four *ratis* — *dāsya*, *sakhya*, *vātsalya*, *mādhurya* — which are normally **exclusive**, and credits Hanuman with all four: *sakhya* at the Vibhīṣaṇa war council where he speaks last without flattery, *vātsalya* in lifting Rāma onto his shoulders, *dāsya* throughout. ⭐ **Then the inversion**: *mādhurya* subdivides into *svakīyā* and *parakīyā*, the second ranked higher because it carries no legitimate claim on the beloved's support — and **Hanuman's *dāsya* exceeds even that**, because *"even the *parakīyā* lover still requires food, clothing and shelter"* while he **chose a monkey's body specifically to need none of them**, living on forest fruit under trees. ⚑ **Selflessness measured by claims has a floor, and the floor is the body.** 🔴 **The same physical fact Akhaṇḍānand (*Character & Virtue* 7) uses to argue the vanara form removes the grounds of *comparison* — caste, appearance, diet — is here used to argue it removes material *need*. Two contributors, one fact, two independent arguments, neither citing the other.** Also the register-marking: *parakīyā* is *"rightly frowned upon in ordinary human life"* and referenced by teachers as *"a spiritual ideal, not a literal model for conduct"*

concepts.title: Separation Without Deprivation
concepts.description: *mādhurya* subdivides again into ***sanyoga*** (union) and ***viyoga*** (separation), **with separation ranked the more refined** — on the tradition's usual test, that withdrawing the reward reveals what the love was actually running on. ⭐ **Rāmsukhdās credits Hanuman with both at once and without contradiction**: in presence, complete service down to cracking his knuckles when Rāma yawns; in separation, not enduring but **absorbed in hearing and retelling** — *"connoisseur of hearing the Lord's own deeds"* — **appearing freely wherever the story is told.** ⚑ **The essay states the contrast that makes it a finding**: an ordinary devoted wife in separation can only long quietly, while Hanuman experiences **limitless delight.** ⚠ *Sanyoga* and *viyoga* are a **partition, not a spectrum** — nothing is supposed to occupy both cells. **Rāmsukhdās treats him as an exception the theory tolerates; this page argues from his own material that the partition was drawn on the wrong variable** — presence of the beloved, rather than availability of the relationship. **The boon read correctly**: Vālmīki 7.40.17, where he asks not for liberation but for residence as long as the story is told, is then not a request for longevity but for the mechanism that makes separation survivable

concepts.title: The Name Above the Person
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the PRD's flagged *name above the person* tension, sourced, and in the strongest possible setting: Rāma asks Hanuman whether his *name* is dearer to him than he is, and Hanuman answers yes** — with an **operational** reason, that the name *"saves all three worlds, every single day, without fail."* Premnidhi names the position ***rāma-nāma-niṣṭhā***, glossed *"something that works even where the person himself hasn't gone"* — ⚑ **which makes the name an agent rather than an address.** Śatruhanaśaraṇ's extreme form: *"it is my one and only possession, now and forever"* — **not his greatest, his only**, which is substitution rather than emphasis. ⭐ **The weighing image, from the *Ādi Rāmāyaṇa*** (a text new to this build), taught to Nala and Nīla at the bridge: **all mantras together on one scale, the fruits of knowledge and meditation on the other, and Rāma's name alone outweighs both** — a ranking above *jñāna* and *dhyāna* combined. ⭐ **And the accessibility argument, which is the transferable half**: the name requires **no ritual purity, no special time, no elaborate rite, and no prior learning** — four prerequisites waived, converging with the akhāṛā material's note that this worship carries no caste or social restriction whatsoever. Plus the *Hanumatsaṃhitā* (also new), addressing his own tongue

concepts.title: Gītā 11.55 as a Checklist
concepts.description: Rājendra Śarmā takes one verse — *mat-karma-kṛn mat-paramo mad-bhaktaḥ saṅga-varjitaḥ, nirvairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu* — and **applies it as an assessment instrument, producing evidence against each of the five terms** rather than paraphrasing it. ⭐⭐ **And the closing move is the finding: full refuge in *any one* of the five brings the remaining four automatically** — which converts a checklist into a **single entry point** and asserts the terms are not independent. ⚑ **Compare: the four-axis service framework has no such claim, and the modern corpus's twenty axioms have no precedence relation at all.** 🔴 ***Mat-paramaḥ* carries a second attestation of Bharata's arrow** — struck while carrying the Droṇācala, pride *briefly arose* before self-correction, with **Gītā 3.27** invoked and the conclusion that it *"never actually took root"*; **a second contributor, in a different group, conceding the same lapse.** ⚠ **Where the fifth term breaks**: *nirvairatva* in a figure who kills is defended by **liberation theology** — Tāḍakā through Rāvaṇa receive liberation as a direct result, extended to Hanuman's own kills, Makarī and the sage-imposter strangled in his tail. ⚑ **This is the volume's only category for its own recorded costs — and it does not reach them**, since it covers those killed by the incarnation or its agents and says nothing about rākṣasa wives miscarrying indoors from a sound. **The essay reframes rather than resolves, and says so**

concepts.title: Three Roads: Rāga, Anurāga, Virāga
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **one of the fifteen highest-value findings the PRD flagged at the outset, now read in its own essay.** Śyāmākānt Dvivedī reads the whole Sundarkāṇḍa as a treatise on **how peace is obtained**, and finds three answers embodied by three characters: ***rāga*** (craving) — **Rāvaṇa** · ***anurāga*** (devoted love) — **Rāma** · ***virāga*** (dispassion) — **Hanuman**, with *anurāga* glossed as the path Pārvatī takes toward Śiva. ⚑ **The three are one root at three prefixes**, which is what makes them commensurable: *rāga* is bare colouring, *anu-* is attachment that follows rather than seizes, *vi-* is attachment removed. **Outcomes are reported to match methods** — Janaka gains illumination, Rāma flourishing, Rāvaṇa destruction — ⚠ **but Janaka appears in the outcome list without appearing in the method list, a mismatch the essay does not remark on.** Gītā principle cited: abandoning scriptural discipline for personal desire achieves neither success, happiness, nor the highest end. ⚑ **Read as a diagnostic rather than a ranking**, since the third road is precisely the one least available to the person who needs it most

concepts.title: Whose Son Is Vairāgya
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **a genealogy that converts an honorific into a doctrine.** Sītā calls Hanuman *son* and he calls her *mother* throughout the Rāmāyaṇa, and it is normally read as warmth. **Dvivedī recalls an old verse in which *Bhakti* personified describes herself as the mother of two sons — *Jñāna* and *Vairāgya*, both worn thin by the passage of time** — and closes the syllogism: **if Sītā is *śānti*, and peace is devotion in its supreme form, then devotion's two sons are hers; and Hanuman, embodying both, is *literally* her son.** ⚑ **The argument only closes because of an identification made earlier and not flagged as load-bearing: *vairāgya* and *jñāna* are not two virtues he happens to have but one at its terminus** — Patañjali's dispassion as *"complete mastery over craving for anything seen or merely heard"*, with the ***Yoga Bhāṣya*** named as the source for *"the actual outermost edge of knowledge itself"*, which is why he holds *jñānināṃ agragaṇyam*. ⚑ **Dvivedī marks his own register explicitly** — *"not a figure of speech, on this reading, but a genealogy"* — one of five such markings in this group of sixteen. **What it explains**: the reciprocal address the volume uses everywhere and nowhere accounts for

concepts.title: Peace Requires Presence, Not Stillness
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the Aśoka-vāṭikā — the grove whose name means *without sorrow* — with Sītā grieving in it continuously**, taken by Dvivedī as a diagnostic rather than as irony. ***"Peace without God's presence merely mimics peace"***: a **hollow trance** has the phenomenology of peace and none of its resolution, and **Sītā's grief lifts only when the ring arrives — proof of Rāma's remembrance.** ⚑ ***Presence, not stillness alone, is the cure.*** **A direct critique of stillness-based practice**, and it lands hard on the modern corpus's visualisation material, which trains a state and has no term for what the state is supposed to be *of*. ⭐ **Four peace-finders are named in Sundarkāṇḍa alone and none of them arrives by sitting**: Rāma on hearing of Sītā · the dying vanara army at the ocean's edge · Hanuman, receiving directly from peace · and Sītā, given the name, the story and the ring with the name inscribed. ⚑ **Janaka's plowing** read as awakening dormant power at the body's base — *peace requires active foundational practice, not palace-dwelling* — and ***"souls can exist without God but never without peace"***, with **even Rāma, understood as Brahman, undertaking a painful search once Sītā is taken.** ⚠ **The diagnosis is better than the prescription**: it names what hollow peace lacks without supplying a way to obtain the presence

concepts.title: Devotion in the Next Room
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the finding of the *Devotion to Rāma* group.** On Umeś Kumār Śrīvāstava's allegory **Sītā is devotion — and devotion has been resident in Rāvaṇa's palace for months, under his own guard, benefiting him not at all.** ⚑ **She is not distant and not hidden; he can go and look at her, and does.** **Doubt and pride** are named as the blockers, and Hanuman's counsel — *"hold Rāma's feet in your heart, and rule Laṅkā undisturbed forever"* — is **a cure the sick man refuses.** Conclusion: ***"Proximity to devotion was never the same thing as actually receiving it."*** ⚑⚑ **This is, in devotional form, the exact structural point this build has made for four phases about corpora that contain their own answers and never apply them** — the referral clause, the Anonymity Test, the conflict hierarchy, the boundary on the Name. ⭐ **New term: *anapāyinī bhakti***, devotion that never wavers or departs, *"a wish-fulfilling jewel"* granted only to *"the rarest few"* — **with the distinction that being accepted by God and receiving permanent devotion are two different things.** ⚑ And the essay's own closing sequence ends on **revealing his true form to Sītā as proof of faith never performed for anyone's benefit**, which is the Anonymity Test's criterion in devotional form

concepts.title: Faith in the Lord Itself Is Hanuman
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **a wandering saint sees a Hanuman image in Dr. Sureś Candra Seṭh's house, asks whether Hanuman is his chosen deity, and says *"faith in the Lord itself is Hanuman."*** ⚑ **Not a compliment about a devotee but a claim about what kind of thing he is — and the kind it names is not *person*.** Devotion has three parts, devotee, object and relation; **the sentence collapses the middle into the third**, so anybody exercising faith in Rāma is *doing* Hanuman rather than addressing him. ⭐ **This is the sourced anchor for the extension corpus's Model 1** — *Hanuman represents the devotional capacity itself, not another object of devotion* — which the PRD flagged and which the build had recorded as *"strong and not yet fully sourced"*, noting the essays developing it sat in groups not yet built. **Contributor, title and page now attached.** ⚠ **It does not rescue that construct's argument**, which runs through an absence in a modern deity roster. 🔴 **And the same one page carries the hardest form of the routing claim — *"Hanuman guards Rāma's own door, and no one enters that court without his permission first"*** — **a gate rather than a preference**, with Premnidhi supplying the motive: **jealous protectiveness over how Rāma's attention gets spent, with wounded feelings when devotees bypass him.** ⚑ **The two claims require different metaphysics and the essay never puts them together: a gatekeeper who can be slighted is a party rather than a function, and the identification has quietly lapsed.** Also **Śaraṇānand's faith / thought / action with faith primary — a rare intra-volume citation**, essay 5 of the same group — and the closing promise of eight siddhis and nine treasures evidenced by **one man, Ramakrishna**, who is the most-recorded religious life of the period and therefore the worst available sample. 🚩 SINGLE SOURCE on both headline claims, the first at a second remove as reported speech

concepts.title: The Complaint Padas and Their Defence
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **six *padas*, almost all Tulsīdās's *Vinaya Patrikā* 31–36, personally selected and paraphrased by Bhāījī Hanumānprasād Poddār — *Kalyāṇ*'s founding editor** — tracing praise, a devotee catching himself mid-complaint, then begging forgiveness. 🔴 **Pada 32 asks whether Hanuman's strength has vanished *or whether pride has appeared in him*** — a charge of moral degradation against the figure twenty-one essays establish as never proud. **Pada 33 makes the same complaint as comedy** (*his power could make tamarind seeds pass as coin — so why is my corner still dark?*) and then **relocates the fault**, conceding only his own heart could have caused the separation. ⭐⭐⭐ **Padas 34–35 are a working philosophy of the complaint, and it is the transferable half**: do not fault the intensely pained, **the selfish**, the humble or the sorrowful for unweighed words · **farmers curse fate over rain without giving divine offence** · Kali Yuga justified the rashness · **genuine trouble prompts remembering capable protectors, so the complaint is itself evidence of faith** · good masters overlook servants' faults. ⚠ **The fourth move has no failure mode** — silence would prove commitment on the same reasoning — **and the second is better because it is narrower**, a claim about speech-acts that could come out wrong. ⚑ **The direct refutation of the extension corpus's premise that traditional bhakti admits only pure emotions**, and it differs in kind from the volume's other two: this is the material *curated deliberately, with a defence attached.* ⚠ **The defence is narrower than it looks** — duress plus an intact relationship — and Tulsīdās's grace is marked *"uniquely unconditional, unearned"*

concepts.title: A Jealous Kind of Grace
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the motive `the-boundary-on-the-name`'s Live Edge asked for and could not find.** Premnidhi: **old ritual texts describe Hanuman as permanently watchful**, and **worship manuals instruct devotees to *"please Hanuman fully first"* — *"not as formality"*** but because his Rāma-devotion includes ***"jealous protectiveness over how Rāma's attention gets spent"*** — ⚑ **with wounded feelings when devotees bypass him with minor requests.** **Neither humility nor institutional self-establishment**: the interest defended is **Rāma's attention**, and the master is the party being managed, by a policy nobody records him instituting. ⚑ **And it is the only motive that predicts the compliance step** — humility generates no requirement, self-establishment wants temples rather than *sequence*, and a filter is what a protective intermediary installs. ⚠ **Which makes the most flattering motive the most corrosive**: ordinary institutional interest can be priced, and **a rule that can be *hurt* produces a debt rather than a penalty** — debts have no discharge condition. ⚑ **The three self-imposed imprecations run the same exclusivity inward** — death's staff for bowing to another, a serpent's bite for other mantras, a thunderbolt for turning his heart elsewhere — **so he is not exempting himself.** 🚩 SINGLE SOURCE; **no manual is named**, which is the cheapest available upgrade to the whole routing cluster

concepts.title: Devotion Before the Meeting
concepts.description: Vaidya Gurudatt argues the Ṛṣyamūka meeting **confirmed** a devotion rather than creating it, and his evidence is about **how far Rāma's reputation had already travelled**: the renunciation — *"giving up a kingdom and walking into fourteen years of exile"* — **reaching Śabarī's remote forest hermitage before Rāma did**, ⚑ **with a deliberately paired second instance, Vibhīṣaṇa's identical physical response on merely hearing the story in Laṅkā.** `[n=2]`. ⭐ **What travelled was a *refusal*** — not the archery, the lineage or the divinity — **and that is the property that let it travel**: a man walking away from a throne is legible in one sentence to anybody, where positional prestige means nothing outside the polity that confers it. ⚑ **Speed explains the collapse at Ṛṣyamūka**: assessment is incremental, confirmation is instant. ⚠ **And the licensing doctrine removes every check the volume elsewhere insists on** — ***sincere faith directed at any form becomes stabilised by God himself***, so aiming is not the devotee's problem, **which makes a true report and a false one identical in effect.** 🔴 Against the same volume's evidentiary tiers and its demand for unstageable proof from Vibhīṣaṇa. ⚠ **A selection artefact**: the hearers who did nothing are not in the record and cannot be. ⚑ Also **a second version of the Gītā's four devotee classes** — *the merely curious* where Śarmā has *the seeker of knowledge*

concepts.title: Only You Can Say Whether That's Flattery
concepts.description: ⭐⭐⭐ **the strongest self-qualification found anywhere in this build.** Having sworn exclusive devotion under three self-imposed curses, Premnidhi's Hanuman says of the whole profession: ***"whether that's the plain truth or empty flattery, only you can really say; let everyone else judge as they will."*** ⚑ **He does not hedge the vow — he leaves it at full strength and disclaims his own standing to score it**, which is a claim about **access** rather than about sincerity. ⚑ **And the claim is true for a non-mystical reason**: flattery of the kind that matters is not conscious lying, so introspection returns the story the mind has already built; while an observer has only behaviour, and **the volume's own spies demonstrate that a subject managing his appearance defeats external assessment** — *"the weakest monkey in the entire army."* ⚑ **The concession is mild evidence *against* the hypothesis it raises**, since flattery aimed at an effect does not come with a disclaimer attached. ⚠ **And the same move is an evasion when it removes an auditor's ground rather than the speaker's** — the direction is the only thing separating discipline from escape hatch. ⚑ **This is the limit the modern corpus's self-scored instruments went without**, four hundred pages away in one sentence. ⚠ 🚩 SINGLE SOURCE, no locator, and the same essay makes the group's most unverifiable assertions

concepts.title: The Debt That Must Not Be Repaid
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ Rāma has nothing equivalent to give and offers **an embrace and unreserved affection**; then says he **would give his life for any single favour and refuses ever to be free of the accumulated debt.** ⚑ **The reason is one line: *"a debt only gets repaid when the person who's owed falls into hardship."*** Service is a **response to need**, so repayment requires an equivalent need — **which means wanting to clear the account is wanting the benefactor in trouble, and remaining indebted is the honour.** ⚑ **Praise delivered entirely as a refusal**, and the only form that cannot read as condescension from a master to a servant. ⚑ **The corollary explains the embrace**: *"for someone whose heart is already full, the only fitting gift left is love itself"* — **a being with no needs cannot be given anything**, and affection is the one transfer with no prerequisite. ⚠ **The argument only holds if repayment must be equivalent *in kind***, which the essay assumes; the volume records real conferrals — a necklace, a boon, agelessness — none needing a crisis. ⚠ **And the sound version is the one the essay does not use**: the needs-nothing property blocks repayment without generalising, where the misfortune argument generalises to any subordinate and reads, from the benefactor's mouth, as a reason never to seek parity

concepts.title: The Jñānī-Bhakta Is God's Very Self
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the fifth attestation of the identification and the only one *argued*.** Vaidya Gurudatt: following the Gītā, **the *jñānī-bhakta* is *"God's very self"***; Hanuman is in that class, in the fourth and highest of the four devotee types; **therefore he is Rāma's own self expressed again.** ⚑ ***Vastutas tvam evāham* reached through a devotee taxonomy and a syllogism rather than through tantric identification** — which means the summit was **available from ordinary premises and the road was public**, making the extension corpus's sense of trespass less warranted still. ⚑ **And a conclusion from *class membership* confers nothing personal** — it is a fact about a category, not an attainment — **which is the version hardest to inflate on, and it went unused.** ⚠ **Everything turns on an unsourced premise**: no verse is given, and whether *the jñānī is God's own self* is the Gītā's phrasing or a commentator's has not been checked. 🔴 **The same essay also asserts acquisition by absorption** — a devotee absorbed enough **shares the deity's qualities**, his valour *reflecting* Rāma's — **which needs two objects where the identity claim leaves one.** ⚑ Plus ***a voice from three places***: no grammatical error and **no facial hesitation**, with the Sanskrit teaching that voice emerges from heart, throat and head together — **hesitation being what cannot be rehearsed**

concepts.title: He Speaks Last
concepts.description: **the same position in the speaking order at three gatherings, from three contributors who cite neither each other nor the pattern.** `[n=3]` **The ocean** (silent until Jāmbavān names him) · **the Vibhīṣaṇa war council** (Rāmsukhdās: *"speaks last, plainly, without flattery or self-interest"*) · **and Mount Suvela, with a locator — *Mānas* 6.12** — where Rāma asks why the moon has a dark patch, each companion offers a theory, and **Hanuman answers last and *replaces the question***: the moon is Rāma's servant and carries *"your own beautiful dark form."* ⚑ **A reframing requires the frame, so the position is a precondition rather than modesty.** ⚑⚑ **And the format is the variable the volume misses**: a chaired round guarantees a turn and a volunteering call does not — **so the identical restraint is a strategy at Suvela and abstention at the shore**, which is why the mission stalls there. ⚠ **Three incompatible explanations for one behaviour** — a curse, a discipline, and no comment at all. ⚑ **This also repairs the moon's-dark-mark material, which Śukratna gives bare**: the image was never the point, the *move* was, and an extracted line loses exactly what made it worth extracting

concepts.title: Love as Service, Service as Love
concepts.description: Rāmāśrayaprasād Siṅh closes the group by taking Karpātrī's **two bees, one lotus** seriously: **Bharata and Hanuman reach one devotion by opposite roads** — **renunciation** (which presupposes possession) against **non-departure** (which presupposes arrival). ⚑ **Symbolic geography as argument**: Bharata's journey **earthly, communal, in the realm of feeling**; Hanuman's **skyward through *cidākāśa*, and solitary** — so one devotion is witnessed throughout and the other has no witness at all until he lands. ⭐⭐ **The closing chiasmus: *"Bharata is love embodied as service; Hanuman is service embodied as love"*** — **and its halves survive being separated**, which is the test a chiasmus usually fails. 🔴 **Two recognitions contrasted — Citrakūṭ as total silence, Ṛṣyamūka as searching questions ending in self-reproach** — **which contradicts Śrīvāstava's instant wordless recognition of the same scene. Both preserved.** ⚑ **Bharata confesses shame at having failed to help *as Rāma's servant***, which means the renouncer envies the servant. ⚑ **The ocean image is precise rather than decorative**: Bharata's character exceeds the physical ocean, *"which mortals have dug, churned, crossed, dammed and drunk dry"* — five verbs, every one a thing somebody in this literature did. ⚠ **The symmetry makes both roads unenterable, and only one half has a recorded cost**

concepts.title: The Plate Run and the Lost Essay
concepts.description: ⚑ **pages 36–43 of the volume are full-page devotional illustration plates with captions and no body text**, and *"Hanuman's Self-Surrender to Rāma"* — **author unknown** — **survives only as a closing fragment on p. 44**, which the modern edition's translator's note records as *"largely lost to a run of illustration plates."* ⚑⚑ **The loss is the finding.** Every count in this phase — three self-markings in sixteen, no essay repeating the boundary teaching — **is a count over fifteen essays and a paragraph**, and the vault says so once here rather than letting the qualification vanish into *read in full*. ⭐ **What survives is not the least valuable part**: a **two-clause servant instruction** (full confidence in the master's greatness, paired with vigilance that one's own conduct never reflects poorly on him) and the term ***tat-sukha-sukhitva*** — the highest devotion as **finding one's own happiness entirely within the lord's happiness** — which is what makes the two clauses cohere, and which supplies **no entry step to anybody not already in the state.** ⚠ **The volume's one genuinely unattributable claim**: the correction that *"the Aṅka says"* cannot refer has nobody here to redirect to. ⚠ `[n=1]` on the observation that the displaced essay is the anonymous one

concepts.title: Verification as Disconfirmation
concepts.description: ⭐⭐⭐ **the sharpest instrument in the group, and it is structurally the inverse of everything the extension corpus builds.** Svāmī Śaraṇānand: ***checking afterwards whether the surrender "worked" is itself evidence that the trust was incomplete.*** ⚑ **A self-referential criterion — running it returns a failure by construction**, so it has no passing state and is a diagnosis rather than a test. ⚑ **And the two failures are not symmetric**: a bad instrument can be repaired (comparison arm, an observable the subject does not generate, a scorer with no stake); **a criterion that convicts the checker cannot be, because the repair would be a check.** ⚠ **The essay then quotes a track record** — people trust timetables *"despite repeated worldly failures and zero divine failures"* — ⚑ **which is a count taken after every witness was disqualified**: the asymmetry is in checkability, not in reliability. ⭐⭐ **The faculty error is the better half**: directing mind, senses and intellect at God **while keeping the self separate** fails, because *"love belongs to the person, the self, not to any one faculty"* — **a practice that feels complete from inside and is not.** 🔴 **And the grace mechanism cuts against the group it sits in**: God does not come *"through that soul's own effort"* but **melts in response to longing** — effort produces nothing — **printed among sixteen essays about service performed.** ⚠ **The essay contains no Hanuman references at all**, and the placement asserts an exclusivity the group's own material contradicts

concepts.title: Two Readings of One Text
concepts.description: 🔴🔴 **the group's headline contradiction, and the sharpest in the build.** **Gopīnāth Tivārī** reads the ***Hanumān Nāṭaka*** as *"pride played straight, without any of the self-effacement that defines Hanuman elsewhere"*; **Sureś Vrat Rāi**, on the same fourteen-act play, records **no boasting anywhere** and has it **end with Hanuman crediting everything to Rāma.** ⚑ **Both are describing one speech** — *"shall I drink the ocean dry, or simply bring Laṅkā itself back here, Rāvaṇa and Sītā included?"* — **and split on the tone word alone**: *"an almost absurd menu of options"* against *"delighted."* ⚑⚑ **Worse than four unshared standards, because disjoint sources can all be right and this cannot**: two readers, one text, a fact of the matter. ⚠ **And the volume's licences do not cover it** — *arthavāda* and kalpa-plurality hold incompatible **positions**, not incompatible **reports.** ⭐ **The missing criterion**: an extravagant declaration is an **oath** when it commits the speaker and a **boast** when it merely advertises him — Nandanandānanda insists the crossing-vow is an oath and the *Nāṭaka*'s near-identical menu is called pride — **and no contributor runs the test.** ⚑ **Two candidate resolutions preserved, neither asserted**: a performative register, or the two essays weighting different acts of the same play. ⚠ **Neither essay quotes a line of it**

concepts.title: Being Told What You Are
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **Jāmbavān names Hanuman twice, in two texts, with opposite consequences.** At the ocean he **recites a record** — parentage, the cursed apsara, Vāyu's promise, the leap at the sun, *your gati outruns every creature's* — and **capability returns**, producing an estimate: ten thousand yojanas. In the *Nāṭaka* he names a **status** — *you are an incarnation of Rudra* — and **restraint departs**, producing not a number but a **menu**. ⚑⚑ **A record restores *information* and leaves the estimate to be made; a status supplies a *warrant*, which has no upper bound, no way of being checked against a task, and nothing in it that says stop.** ⭐ **And the curse has a verse at last — *Vālmīki 7.35.16*** — with Nandanandānanda correcting the morale reading outright: the restoration was **literal curse-lifting**, not encouragement. ⚑ **He performs the reminding operation on Sugrīva, competently, while under the condition himself.** ⚠ **The register of a naming is not usually chosen — it is dictated by what the namer believes**, so anybody convinced a colleague is exceptional *by nature* finds the record register unavailable

concepts.title: The Third Lapse Is Vālmīki's
concepts.description: 🔴🔴 **a third conceded lapse, larger than the two on record, and it is the poet's rather than a contributor's.** **Vālmīki labels the mendicant disguise *śaṭha-buddhi* — foolish cunning** — in a poem that *"will go on to praise Hanuman's intelligence everywhere else."* And in Rāvaṇa's chambers, **mistaking the sleeping Mandodarī for Sītā, he loses composure entirely: claps, kisses his own tail, dances, shouts, leaps onto pillars and tumbles back down.** ⚠ **Not the harem waver.** Ciṅgle's is desire against the eightfold standard; this is **dignity, on a mistaken recognition, with relief as the emotion.** **Same room, different axis — do not merge.** ⭐⭐ **And the mechanical finding is the recoveries**: *within a single breath* · *never actually took root* · *settling back into his own natural gravity within moments* — **three contributors, three groups, one manoeuvre.** `[n=3]` ⚑ **A hagiography cannot report a failure; it can report a recovery, and a recovery needs one.** ⚑⚑ **Which means the count of two was never a count of lapses** — it was a count of **places the volume's humility argument met resistance.** **Upādhyāy prints a full-scale Purāṇic boast (Brahma Vaivarta 62.75–76) and files it as *"genuinely striking literary language"***, because a survey essay has no thesis for it to damage

concepts.title: A Sin, an Expiation, a Shrine
concepts.description: ⭐⭐⭐ **the category this build kept recording as missing existed in the Purāṇic material all along.** ***Skanda*, Avanti-khaṇḍa 83: Hanuman installs the Hanumanteśvara-liṅga on the Narmadā in expiation for killing a Brahmin** — *brahmahatyā*, the paradigm case of the gravest class of offence — **with Kapitīrtha established in ch. 84 and two further liṅgas installed by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.** **And a second, separate atonement in *Brahma Vaivarta*, Brahma-khaṇḍa 46, for killing Rāvaṇa.** ⚑⚑ **A justification removes a cost; an expiation concedes it, leaves it wrong, and adds an obligation** — which is what a category for cost *is*, and the volume's standard move is the other one. ⚠ **The devotional essays cannot use the instrument**, because an expiation entails a sin their whole argument denies — so the harder material sits in the survey register, again. ⚠⚠ **And it does not reach the costs this build has been recording**: both remedies are built for **deeds with a doer and a victim**, and the battle-cry's miscarriages have neither. **Two independent categories, one gap.** ⚑ **The acknowledgement is a *building* — non-defensive, untellable-otherwise, and it needs nobody to remember anything**

concepts.title: The Liṅga He Could Not Uproot
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the only outright failure of strength in the build, and it has a locator.** *Brahma Vaivarta*, Brahma-khaṇḍa 46: sent to Kailāsa for a liṅga, **he is delayed**; **Sītā fashions one from sand to save the auspicious hour**; he returns, **tries to uproot hers, fails, and collapses unconscious.** ⚑ **Every other limit in the corpus is somebody's decision** — the offers Rāma declines to commission, the envoy's brief, the vow. **This one is not accepted, and therefore cannot be converted into evidence of restraint** — which is why thirty-seven devotional essays never mention it. **It is not embarrassing; it is *unusable*.** ⚑ **The motive is stated: distress at what he perceived as *"Śiva's own dishonour"*** — the same protectiveness Premnidhi records over Rāma's attention, pointed at another god and producing an action. ⚠ **He is revived by his praises being recited** — the third time in one group that reciting what he is does something to him. ⭐ **And Sītā's improvisation is the story's real achievement**: she optimises for the constraint that cannot move, and the tradition ratifies it by making her sand **immovable**

concepts.title: The Non-Celibate Hanuman
concepts.description: 🔴🔴 ***"He was never a lifelong celibate at all — he lived a full householder's life first."*** Tāranchand Paṇḍyā: asceticism taken up **at life's end**, renouncing **kingdom, possessions and wife together**, with **liberation in that same lifetime on the strength of the renouncing.** ⚑ **The two accounts are not degrees of one thing**: a **maintained state** is damaged by any breach — which is why the harem search is a crisis when the vow's first article is a gaze — and **a completed act is not damaged by what preceded it.** They disagree about what the liberating event *is*. ⭐ **A formal rank in a closed enumeration**: sixty-three exalted souls, plus twenty-four **Kāmadevas**, of whom Hanuman is the **eighteenth**, with liberation guaranteed by the rank — **the only placement in the build that could be wrong in a checkable way.** ⭐ **And a *Vidyādhara*, not a vanara at all** — a fourth answer that dissolves the species question instead of answering it. ⚠ **He is precise about timing and silent on everything checkable**: no wife named, no children, no kingdom located. ⚠⚠ **The contradiction is never articulated inside the volume** — Paṇḍyā brackets his claim, names neither Vālmīki nor Tulsīdās, and states no competing position. ⚑ **PRD CORRECTED: this is essay 9 alone; essay 8 contains none of it**

concepts.title: He Wrote a Book, or He Was Quoted in Books
concepts.description: 🔴 **two music essays, consecutive pages, opposite claims, zero shared citations.** **Avasthī**: Hanuman **wrote** the ***Āñjaneya-saṃhitā* / *Hanumat-saṃhitā***, lost, reconstructed through **Raghunātha of Tanjore (17c, *Saṅgīta-sudhā*)**, **Śārṅgadeva (13c, *Saṅgīta-Ratnākara*)** and **Śāradātanaya's transmission chain.** **Sāhi**: he wrote nothing — three treatises **cite** him, with **Kālinda naming *Śiva-mata*, *Bharata-mata* and *Hanuman-mata***, and **seven ornaments each introduced *"Hanuman says."*** ⚑ **The weaker bibliography makes the stronger claim**: a named *school* survives a book's loss, and transmitted practice leaves procedures rather than doctrines. ⭐⭐ **Eighteen *śruti* intervals against the mainstream twenty-two** — **falsifiable, minority, and not about him**, which is unlike every other claim in this build and *costs* the attributor something. ⭐ **Sāhi's is the finest register-marking in the build**: *"whatever the historical truth of the attribution, an entire specialist tradition kept finding it worth citing his name."* ⚠ **Rāvaṇa appears in both rosters as a master of the art** `[n=2]`. ⚠ **Title collision flagged, not resolved**: a *Hanumatsaṃhitā* in which he addresses his own tongue is a devotional text

concepts.title: Doctrine Shaped by Careful Listening
concepts.description: ⭐⭐⭐ **the epistemology the volume's other domains lack, sitting in its music essay.** Working musicians produced regional performance notes **violating the fixed rules on microtonal density and achieving the correct emotional effect anyway** — and the sage **Yaṣṭika**, rather than force practice to match rule, **updated the theory to match audible practice.** ⚑ ***"Doctrine shaped by careful listening rather than the reverse."*** ⚑ **The anomaly was treated as evidence *about* the rule rather than as an exception *to* it**, and the arbiter is **the effect** — external to the doctrine, available to non-experts, and able to come out negative. ⚑⚑ **Three domains, three epistemologies, one volume**: **bhakti forbids checking** (running the test is the failure), **statecraft cites nothing** (lore has no locus to revise), **music amends.** **No contributor notices.** ⚑ **And the difference is structural, not moral**: a performance has an outcome outside the claimant and a claim about one's own surrender does not — **so the modern corpus's instruments are aimed at a domain with no arbiter, using a design that needs one.** ⚠ `[n=1]`, **with no case recorded where the listening produced a refusal** — and a resolution with no stated limit is a licence rather than a method

concepts.title: Convening Without One Word of Comment
concepts.description: **three boundary crossings, no editorial note anywhere.** `[n=3]` **A Jain monastic placed among the *character* essays rather than in the comparative section** — coverage becoming testimony by placement. **Guru Gobind Siṅh's own Rāmāyaṇa**, with the Guru's **self-recorded date inside the text** (*V.S.* 1758, Anandpur Sāhib) — **the strongest provenance in the build** — printed as unremarkable. **And Surdās, the canonical Kṛṣṇa poet, surveyed for his Rāma *padas*** with no mention of the *Sūr Sāgar*, no comparison to Tulsīdās, and no word about the sectarian boundary — ⚑ **while his Hanuman calls Rāma *Murāri*, a Kṛṣṇa epithet, and neither poet nor essayist remarks on it.** ⚑ **The volume argues by *arrangement*, which is powerful and completely uncitable** — a reader cannot quote a table of contents, and any anthologist reordering would silently undo it. 🔴 **Two readings preserved**: **confidence** (a secure tradition does not announce its guests) or **absorption** (unmarked inclusion is how a majority takes material in without conceding). ⚠ **Three genres arriving at one omission suggests a venue expectation rather than three choices**

concepts.title: Molla Moves Laṅkinī
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the first objection to the guṇa allegory that comes from a text rather than from reasoning.** Of three fourteenth-century Telugu Rāmāyaṇas, **Molla delays the Laṅkinī confrontation until *after* the Aśoka grove is destroyed and the city burned** — *"a genuinely different sequence of events, not just a different emphasis."* ⚑ **The allegory's strength was that the correspondence is *in the geometry*** — three obstacles at three heights, in sequence, on the way in. **In Molla the geometry survives and the sequence does not**, and a rājasika tendency met after the mission is complete is not a stage of a passage. ⚠ **Worse than general instability**: Maināka, Surasā and Siṃhikā are **near-identical across all three**, so the transmission is firm where the allegory needs it least and mobile exactly at its middle term. ⚑ **An incoherence can be answered with a better statement; a missing feature cannot** — the allegory is a reading of the **majority sequence** and the volume nowhere says so. ⭐ **But the three *methods* survive the reordering**, which shows the doctrine was **prior** and the episodes were the illustration — the causation the volume's contributors have backwards. ⚑ **And the essay contains no guṇa mapping at all**, eliminating this group as the PRD claim's source

concepts.title: Recognition With a Stated Criterion
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the *Bhāskara Rāmāyaṇa* supplies the specification the volume's recognition material asserts and never gives.** Hanuman performs **austerities for Brahmā** and receives a boon: ***whoever can actually see the ornaments adorning his body will be recognised as his true master and the one capable of granting him liberation*** — paying off at Ṛṣyamūka, where **Rāma, disguised as a Brahmin at Sugrīva's request, sees both his true vanara nature and the hidden ornaments.** ⚑⚑ **And the direction reverses**: everywhere else in this build *Hanuman* recognises *Rāma*; **the boon exists because he cannot.** ⭐ **Four properties nothing else in the build has**: set **in advance**, by a **third party with no stake**, **involuntary on the candidate's side**, and **binary**. ⚠ **A faculty is unfalsifiable** — every instance is a success, because a failure would not be reported as an instance. ⚑ **And both parties are in disguise**, with Rāma seeing through Hanuman's and Hanuman not seeing through Rāma's — which makes Vālmīki's *śaṭha-buddhi* verdict on that disguise not merely improper but pointless. ⚠ No recorded failure; `[n=1]`. Molla does not spell it out

concepts.title: The Envoy's Limit in His Own Mouth
concepts.description: ⭐⭐⭐ **the strongest form of the envoy-limits doctrine in the build, and it comes from a Kṛṣṇa poet.** In the grove Surdās's Hanuman lists what he could do — **tear Laṅkā loose and carry it to her father's kingdom · slaughter every night-wandering demon · send Rāvaṇa to the underworld · unite her with Rāma this very instant, since the army already waits at the ocean's edge** — ***"except that I'm afraid of overstepping the order I was actually given."*** ⚑ **Jāmbavān states the limit in advance and costs nothing; Akhaṇḍānand praises exceeding it. Surdās has the limit voiced by the party it binds, at maximum temptation, with the capability present** — and what he is paying is the rescue. 🔴 **And the same envoy destroys a garden nobody sent him to destroy**, which by scale is the larger breach — **so the operative rule is not *stay inside the brief*, and the volume never says what it is.** ⚠ **The restraint has a body count and no essay prices it.** 🔴 Against Sītā's own refusal to be carried, which is a different constraint on different grounds — **and neither protects Sītā.** ⚑ Also **n=3 for the trust motive** in the language question

concepts.title: The Door Pada Read Two Ways
concepts.description: ⚠⚠ **the build's hardest routing claim rests on a paraphrase, and the line's own specialist reads it the other way.** Seṭh: *"Hanuman guards Rāma's own door, and no one enters that court without his permission first."* **Bhikṣu Ānand, on Tulsīdās's *Rām duāre tum rakhvāre*, paraphrases it as asking any devotee who wants to reach Rāma to embody *the exact renunciation of self*.** ⚑ **Permission against imitation** — different operative party, different requirement, different meaning of failure — **and the second has no intermediary in it at all.** 🚩 **So the *function* is five-source and uncontested; the *gate* is single-source and contested.** ⚑ **And the gate reading travels because it generates practice** — a prior worship, an order of approach, *please Hanuman fully first* — **while an exhortation generates nothing institutional**, so its prevalence is evidence about carriers rather than about meaning. ⚠ Neither essay locates the pada

concepts.title: Inadequacy, Not Refusal
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **three attestations of the permanent debt, and all three say the same thing, and it is not what this build said.** From the *Mānas*: **no one — god, man or sage — has ever done him a greater service, and *he cannot imagine how to repay it***; Rāma **weeping, trembling, looking at Hanuman again and again**, trying repeatedly to lift him and finally placing his hand on his head. Tivārī: **permanently in his debt**, and no other figure receives that honour. Nandanandānanda: *"by whose valour we, and all fourteen worlds, stand in his debt."* ⚠⚠ **None says *refuses*.** ⚑ **The misfortune argument — that repayment requires the creditor's hardship, so remaining indebted is the honour — is Premnidhi's own construction**, and this build carried it for a phase as the tradition's position. ⚑ **The correction cost one paragraph because the earlier page had already isolated the clause as his** — which is the whole value of recording whose words a formulation is. ⭐ And the scene's frame is **Śiva telling it to Pārvatī**

concepts.title: Tulsīdās Never Says It
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **the volume's Tulsīdās specialist says the *Mānas* never states the Śiva identification.** It narrates gods descending in vanara form and ***"never actually specifies which god took which form"***; the familiar assignments (Jāmbavān as Bṛhaspati, Nala/Nīla as the Aśvins) are **flagged in the essay as editorial speculation**; and the whole textual base is **one epithet — *Āśutoṣ*, at one scene** — called *"a small but pointed word choice."* ⚑⚑ **Which inverts the attestation order against the influence order**: the identity is **stated outright with chapter numbers in the Purāṇas** and **absent from the poem that founded the cult.** ⚠ **The largest claim rests on a shrine**: Saṅkaṭmocan in Kāśī, from which *"what's actually being worshipped, nationwide, is Śiva himself under another name"* — an inference with no step in it, since everything in Kāśī is in Śiva's city. ⚑ **And the volume has a reason to want it unstated: a Hanuman who *is* Śiva is not a devotee**, which the whole *dāsya* apparatus needs him to be. 🔴 Two Aṅgadas

concepts.title: Four Lines of Tamil
concepts.description: ⚠ **the volume's entire Tamil coverage is one *dhyāna* verse of four lines**, with no dates for Kamban, no context, no comparison, nothing on the Āḻvārs, and no other stanza. ⭐⭐ **And the verse is a gem**: ***añjile oṇṟu***, *one among the five*, **repeated exactly five times, once per element in sequence — wind, water, sky, earth, fire** — with **Hanuman, the ocean, Sītā and Laṅkā all named by not being named.** ⚑ **Compression by *suppression* rather than by *selection***: nothing is discarded and only the names are removed, so the verse is complete for a reciter who knows the story and opaque to anyone who does not. **A filter rather than a summary**, which is correct for a meditation-verse. ⚑ **Also a mnemonic**: a repeated formula with five slots fixes the order and breaks visibly when corrupted — which the volume's own lists (seven registers, four axes, eight fruits) do not. ⚠⚠ **And the comparative section mostly does not compare — three essays of eighteen — and every structural finding in the phase came from those three**

concepts.title: The Moderns Decide the Split
concepts.description: **two twentieth-century Hindi poets settle, without argument, what the volume cannot.** Maithilī Śaraṇ Gupt's *Sāket* and Baldev Prasād Miśra's *Rām-Rājya* reconstruct Hanuman as **fully human**, grounding the feats in **spiritual discipline and yogic attainment rather than divine machinery** — ⚑ **and retaining the eight siddhis**, which is the combination the volume never assembles, because it needs **endowment for worship and attainment for exhortation.** ⚑ **Not a reduction but a *relocation*:** the ocean is still crossed, and what changes is the cause — **a theology of descent swapped for a technology of practice**, which is what the *Yoga Sūtra* apparatus already offered. ⚠ **Which incurs a debt — an account of the discipline — and the essay does not say whether the poets pay it.** ⚑ **And the nationalism relocates**: the volume's *rāṣṭravīr* turn is in the **devotional** essays and is entirely absent from the one essay on modern verse. ⚠ `[n=2]`, selected, undated, no poem quoted

concepts.title: The Celibate and the Hundred Sons
concepts.description: ⚑ ***Hanumatkuṇḍ*, a tīrtha on Gandhamādana founded by Hanuman, where King Dharmaśākha obtained a hundred sons from his hundred wives** through a rite and then attained heaven — reported in a list of bathing-places, at the weight of a place-name, by a volume that spends twenty-one essays on lifelong *brahmacarya*. Plus the Jain classification among the **twenty-four *Kāmadevas***. `[n=2]`, four hundred pages apart, neither remarked on. ⚠⚠ **NOT a contradiction**: ascetic continence converting into another party's fertility is entirely standard, **and the finding is that no contributor builds the bridge** — because none of them is looking at the shrine. ⚑ **A shrine's advertised efficacy records the *traffic*, not the doctrine** — and the traffic places Hanuman in the ordinary petitionary economy the apotropaic cluster already documents. ⚠ **Both items single-source and unlocated; the *Kāmadeva* sense is unknown to this build and is carried as a collocation, not an argument**

concepts.title: The Siddhis Disarmed in Public
concepts.description: the extension corpus prints each of the eight *aṣṭavarga* powers twice, *"Traditional"* above *"Daily Life Equivalent"*, and **both of the powers over other people come out as qualities of the self**: ***īśitva*, "natural commanding power over others," becomes leadership; *vaśitva*, "power to control others through will," becomes "the magnetism of being authentically yourself"** — closing on a practice note that tells the reader not to manipulate. ⚑⚑ **Deliberate disarmament, performed in public with the original left visible beside it**, and it is **Pāṭhak's inward-redirection requirement rebuilt from scratch by someone who had never read it** — a third independent arrival alongside the Aurobindo self-governance reading. `[n=3]` across three centuries and no contact. ⚠⚠ **But a conversion is not a prohibition, and a conversion has no slot to put one in**: once *vaśitva* means authenticity, *"do not use vaśitva on people"* has nothing to attach to. **So nothing catches the corpus's own outward-aimed fierce practice**, and the missing sentence is a consequence of choosing replacement over condition rather than an oversight

concepts.title: The Deity as a Variable
concepts.description: one clause in the extension corpus makes the object of devotion an input: *"If you're drawn to other spiritual focuses, adapt this approach accordingly."* ⚠ **Against *ananya***, against Hazārīprasād Dvivedī's verse widening the *served* so the *server's* attachment need not widen, and against Premnidhi's exclusive vow sworn under three self-imposed curses. ⚑⚑ **But the substitution survives technique by technique rather than wholesale**: a gratitude ritual consumes none of the figure's particular content, archetypal identification consumes almost all of it — **so portability tracks how much of Hanumān a given technique was using, which is a sharper result than either "the corpus violates *ananya*" or "the method is portable."** ⚑ **And the volume half-agrees**: *"faith in the Lord itself is Hanuman"* dissolves the figure into the capacity rather than making it optional. ⚑ **The variable was misnamed — what must hold constant is the *mode*, and *dāsya* is defined by the servant's position rather than by the master's identity.** 🧭 **Live edge, not a defect: neither corpus argues its position, because within each the alternative is invisible**

concepts.title: Two Rosters, and a Rasa He Should Not Have
concepts.description: the flagship runs **eight** rasas including the invented ***karuṇā-vipralambha***, which is *śṛṅgāra*'s separation-mode retained under *karuṇā*'s name with *śṛṅgāra* itself deleted; the rasa document runs the **canonical nine** and assigns Hanumān ***śṛṅgāra*** in the Aśoka grove. ⚠ **That removes the load-bearing member of Rāmsukhdās's inversion**, which ranks *dāsya* above even *parakīyā-mādhurya* precisely because it carries no bodily need whatsoever — **an argument grounded in an absence, inverted by restoring the thing absent.** ⚑ **Neither document mentions the other**: the phase-6 music pair reproduced inside one author. ⚑⚑ **Both rosters are wrong answers to a real problem the tradition had already solved and named — *bhakti-rasa*, which appears in neither.** ⛑ **Correction to this build's own first reading recorded on the page**: the eight-item roster is one document's, not the corpus's, and the suppression reading is refuted

concepts.title: The Content Creation Dīkṣā
concepts.description: the extension corpus's most fully specified practice: a **fifteen-to-twenty-minute east-facing pre-writing initiation in three phases.** **Sacred-space establishment** — *[MANTRA WITHHELD]* ×7, *Om Rāmāya Namaḥ* ×21, *Om Hum Hanumate Namaḥ* ×11, then the Trinity Council triangle with Rāma at twelve o'clock, Hanumān at four, Sītā at eight. **A three-way diagnostic of creative state** — **Liquid** (warm honey through the spine; story content), **Solid** (crystalline in the bones; frameworks), **Gas** (lightness at the crown; vision) — each with a bodily marker. **Mantra charging by content type**, each state selecting one of three Gāyatrīs with its own nyāsa and visualisation. **Plus three real-time phase-switching protocols and a three-phase crisis protocol** for blank-page terror, imposter syndrome and perfectionism paralysis, opening on *"What is aware of this writing crisis?"* and assigning reframe to Rāma, outward redirection to Hanumān and scope-reduction to Sītā. ⚑ **The transferable core is the diagnostic: a forced three-way self-report taken before work begins, in which the answer selects the task rather than the effort** — which inverts the usual relation between plan and state. ⚠ Contradicted in the same document by a fixed Monday/Wednesday/Friday deity rota; the protective mantra is mis-divided here and correct in four sibling files; and the crisis protocol's closing assurance that *"your words serve dharma and cannot cause harm"* would, carried out of context, disarm every check the corpus builds elsewhere

concepts.title: The Before-Writing Arsenal
concepts.description: the extension corpus's **five preparation techniques, each selecting an emotional register before writing begins**, and each specified with a mantra and repetition count, a nyāsa, a four-step visualisation and a list of the content types it serves. **Vīra Rasa Activator** — ×21, right fist on heart, left hand in abhaya-mudrā; Hanumān in warrior form, courage rising the spine *"like molten gold"*; for contrarian frameworks and *"why everyone is wrong about X"*. **Śānta Rasa Stabilizer** — ×108 *"use a mālā if you have one"*, dhyāna-mudrā; Rāma's forest ashram, amrita from the crown; for philosophical deep-dives. **Hāsya Rasa Generator** — ×49 *"chanted with a slight smile"*, hands on the belly *"gently laughing"*; child-Hanumān, laughter *"like champagne effervescence"*; for teaching through joy. **Karuṇā Rasa Opener** — Sītā Gāyatrī ×21 plus *Om Rāmāya Namaḥ* ×21, left hand extended palm-up; **Sītā in the Aśoka grove as the model**; for crisis and healing content. **Raudra Rasa Destroyer** — ×108 *"with intensity"*, tarjanī-mudrā; for exposing predatory practices. ⚑ **Vīra and Raudra share one mantra and differ by count and mudrā — abhaya faces the practitioner's own fear, tarjanī faces outward at a target; the escalation is marked in the hands.** ⚑⚑ **The counts read as doses calibrated to distance from the writer's ordinary state**, and the dīkṣā's three-state diagnostic — in the same document, unconnected — is exactly the instrument that would make the dosing variable. ⚠ Five of eight or nine rasas are routed; *śṛṅgāra*, *adbhuta*, *bhayānaka* and *bībhatsa* have no technique. 🚩 The fierce mantra is mis-divided here, at 108 repetitions

concepts.title: The During-Writing Arsenal
concepts.description: **five techniques that run inside the session**, each with an ***active* nyāsa** — a gesture returned to at specified moments while the writing happens — which makes them **interruption disciplines rather than state inductions.** ⚑⚑ **And each attaches to a different unit of text, which the document never states**: **Vāk-Siddhi Transmission** at the *sentence* (*Om Hanumate Vāk-Siddhaye Namaḥ*, throat touched at each declaration — **the only technique with its own dedicated mantra, and the only one claiming an effect in a reader's memory**) · **Bhakti Flow State** at the *paragraph* (*"How does this serve collective awakening?"* — a purpose check, not a quality check) · **Buddhi Blade** at the *key point* (Hanumān Gāyatrī between major points, third eye touched; ***"Is this serving clarity or just sounding smart?"*** — **the only test in all fifteen techniques a second reader could apply to your page**) · **Māyā Dissolution** at the *section* (both hands briefly on the eyes; *"gentle but persistent logic"* — **argument named as the mechanism**, unlike the corpus's viral-content document) · **Gamana-Śakti Rush** across the *whole draft*, no interval at all. 🔴 **The Blade edits while writing; the Rush forbids it — the two opposed drafting doctrines, both held, neither acknowledging the other**, separated only accidentally by the rasa routing table

concepts.title: The After-Writing Arsenal
concepts.description: **five session-closing rituals, and three are revision protocols disguised as dedications.** **Seva Integration** — *[MANTRA WITHHELD]* ×21 plus ***Sarve bhavantu sukhinaḥ*** ×7 (a genuine verse, conventionally used); hands to the heart then extended in offering; ***"read the entire piece once with heart awareness, not editorial mind."*** **Karma Yoga Completion** — Rāma Gāyatrī ×21 plus ×108; **a four-point check including *"remove anything that's self-serving"* (the system's only deletion instruction) and *"can readers actually implement this?"*** **Hanumān Seal** — the fierce mantra ×49; **the de-escalation matching the Raudra technique's 108**, which is the strongest safety feature in the fifteen. 🚩 Its third step seals the piece *"to reach only those who will benefit"* — **distribution control by intention, standing where a fairness check belongs.** **Sītā Blessing** — Sītā Gāyatrī ×49, hands on the belly then touching the earth; ***"bless your own courage in sharing"* — the only instruction anywhere in the system aimed at the writer's own wellbeing.** **Trinity Synthesis** — three Gāyatrīs at ×21 each plus ×108; **the Council run backwards as a retrospective three-lens audit with a balance check.** ⚑⚑ **This arsenal is the corpus's only revision discipline, and it fires on genre rather than need — so contrarian work, the most exposed output, receives the one ritual with no review step.** 🔴 Seva forbids the editorial mind and Karma Yoga instructs deletion: **a standard revision sequence, filed as genre alternatives so no piece ever gets both**

concepts.title: Strategic Prāṇāyāma
concepts.description: the extension corpus's most physically specified practice, built for decision-making. **Basic (5–15 min)**: east-facing, spine erect, dhyāna-mudrā; sandalwood incense; **a glass of water placed to the right *"representing clarity of perception"*** and never referred to again; and a **4:6 breath carrying the mantra split across the cycle — *"Om Hanu"* on the four-count inhale, *"mate Namaha"* on the six-count exhale**, so that neither the breath nor the mantra can be completed without the other. ⚑ **Step four is the practice's actual content**: *"during each exhalation, consciously release attachment to specific outcomes **while maintaining clear intention about your strategic purpose**"* — the cognitive posture good decisions require, attached to a rhythm rather than to a resolution. **Advanced (15–30 min)**: constitutional breathing, then **four rounds of twenty-seven breaths** — Obstacle Clearing · Intelligence Enhancement · Courage Integration · Service Dedication. ⚑⚑ **Four twenty-sevens are one hundred and eight — a full mālā quartered by function — and the document never mentions the total**, leaving open whether the count or the four capacities is primary. ⚠ Three constitutional adaptations, of which the Pitta one names *"competitive spiritual practice"* as a hazard and routes the practitioner to devotional material first — **the only place in the cluster where a practice is withheld from a temperament on grounds of likely misuse.** ⚑ Tracking proposed: decision-latency timing (genuinely measurable), 1–10 stress scaling, and an outcome-quality judgement scored by the same person who classified the state

concepts.title: The Five-Phase Identity Meditation
concepts.description: forty minutes with exact minute markers, and **the most carefully guarded practice in the corpus**. **Ego Dissolution (1–5)** — releasing identity attachments in a widening rather than a negating form (*"I am not **just** my professional role"*), with the guard stated as the phase's key insight: ***"archetypal embodiment requires temporary ego softening rather than ego destruction… without losing functional awareness or practical capability."*** **Quality Activation (6–15)** — devotional service, intelligent strength (*"not aggressive force but confident competence"*) and fearless compassion, **each felt energetically before being visualised**, and each defined against its failure mode. **Archetypal Visualisation (16–25)** — ***"while maintaining your own identity and life circumstances"***; *"divine costume meditation"*, wearing qualities *"like sacred clothing while remaining authentically yourself"*; and ***"you're not pretending to be Hanumān but accessing the Hanumān-consciousness that exists within your own awareness"*** — **the tradition's summit claim arriving as a meditation instruction.** **Challenge Integration (26–35)** — real current problems brought into the expanded state, a full quarter of the practice. **Integration and Dedication (36–40)**, with the stated goal of daily-activity access rather than formal-session access. ⚑⚑ **Four safeguards — temporary, softening not destruction, functional awareness retained, identity and circumstances kept — independently derived without access to the tradition's own limits.** ⚠⚠ **And the corpus's other identification practice, the Full Deity Visualisation embedded in the daily writing ritual, has none of them and instructs *"write AS the deity."*** ⚠ Generation-stage practice conventionally ends in dissolution; this ends in carry-over, which is the point and also the missing guarantee

concepts.title: The Dharmic Morphological Box
concepts.description: **Rāma's sixteen divine qualities from Vālmīki 1.1.2–1.1.4, given with Devanagari, transliteration and gloss** — *guṇavān, vīryavān, dharmajña, kṛtajña, satyavākya, dṛḍhavrata, cāritreṇa yukta, sarvabhūteṣu hita, vidvān, samartha, priyadarśana, ātmavān, jitakrodha, dyutimān, anasūyaka, kasya bibhyati devāḥ* — **crossed with nine life contexts and three mantra modes (Protection as shield, Guidance as compass, Transformation as alchemical agent) to yield 432 "Dharmic Addresses."** ⚑⚑ **The address form is a memory palace the corpus never names as one**: *"Gratitude Palace, Relationship District, Shield Quarter"* maps building/district/quarter onto quality/context/mode, which is why 432 cells are navigable at all. ⭐ **The best-sourced construct in the extension corpus** — named text, chapter-and-verse locator, Devanagari, **and a volunteered hedge distinguishing sixteen *qualities* from sixteen *kalās*.** ⚑ **Carries the corpus's only external verification test (the Nārada Verification Method — *"would Nārada recognise this as authentic Rāma consciousness?"*, with authenticity routed to the epic rather than to feeling), its Vālmīki Integration Protocol pairing qualities to episodes (Kevaṭ the boatman for *kṛtajña*, the bridge for *samartha*), and the only explicit cross-document citation anywhere in the cluster.** ⚠ Four of 432 are worked; the 27/162/432 tiers are asserted; and the sixteenth item is a phrase about the gods' fear rather than a cultivable disposition, which the box multiplies twenty-seven times regardless

concepts.title: The Three-Phase Content Cycle
